text: Financial Services - Financials - Annual Financial Report The University's most recent Annual Financial Report (AFR) is available at the link below: FY25 Annual Financial Report Reporting Entity The AFR contains the consolidated financial statements for Wichita State University and its component units. the Wichita State Innovation Alliance, Inc. (WSIA) has been included in the basic financial statements as a blended component unit. In addition, the following organizations are reported as discretely presented component units: Wichita State University Foundation and Alumni Engagement (Foundation) Wichita State University Intercollegiate Athletic Association (ICAA) Wichita State University Union Corporation (Union Corp) Wichita State University Board of Trustees (Board of Trustees) Wichita State University Campus of Applied Sciences and Technology (WSU Tech) Overview of the AFR The AFR includes the following information: Introductory section: the introductory section includes general information about the University, including a list of principal officials, the University’s current organizational chart and a letter of transmittal. The letter of transmittal includes forward-looking information about the University’s projects and strategic initiatives. Financial section: Management’s Discussion & Analysis (MD&A) – provides an objective analysis of the University’s financial activities, with a focus on a comparison of the current fiscal year to the previous fiscal year. Basic Financial Statements – includes comparative statements for the University and its discretely presented component units: Statement of Net Position – presents the assets, deferred outflows of resources, liabilities, deferred inflows of resources and net position of the University at a point in time (at the end of the fiscal year). Its purpose is to present a financial snapshot of the University. Statement of Revenue, Expenses and Changes in Net Position – presents the activity that occurred during the fiscal year. Revenues earned and expenses incurred during the fiscal year on an accrual basis are classified as either operating or nonoperating. Statement of Cash Flows – presented for the University only, this statement presents sources of changes in cash and cash equivalents. Notes to the Financial Statements – provides additional information about the reporting entity, significant accounting policies and significant classes of transactions. Required Supplementary Information – includes information about the University’s pension and other post-employment benefit plans, which is required for GAAP reporting purposes. Supplementary Information – combining schedules for the University’s discretely presented component units are presented as supplementary information. Financial Statement Audit The University is governed by the Kansas Board of Regents and is an agency of the State of Kansas. As such, the University’s financial statements are consolidated into the State University System and included as a discretely presented component unit in the annual comprehensive financial report (ACFR) of the State of Kansas. Although the University’s stand-alone financial statements do not include an auditor’s opinion, the University’s financial information, which is incorporated into the State’s financial report, is subjected to audit procedures as part of the State’s “aggregate discretely presented component units” opinion unit. For additional information about the results of the State of Kansas audit, please refer to the separately issued ACFR for the State of Kansas available at: https://admin.ks.gov/offices/oar/annual-comprehensive-financial-report---acfr . Single Audit Similar to the University’s financial statement audit, which is completed as part of the State University System, the University’s Single Audit is also completed as part of the State as a whole. Information about the results of the Statewide Single Audit report is available at: https://admin.ks.gov/offices/accounts-reports/state-agencies/finance/annual-comprehensive-financial-report/statewide-single-audit-report . title: RSC Speed Interviews
text: RSC Speed Interviews - Are you looking for part-time employment on campus? The RSC is looking for YOU! We are hiring summer and fall student positions now What to Expect You will be given three minutes to put your best foot forward and make an impression on our hiring managers. Undeniably, speed interviews are less formal than traditional interviews, but that is not an excuse to dress in blue jeans and sneakers. The best approach is to dress professionally. How to Prepare Following the tips below can help make the most of the short meeting time: Bring Documents: up-to-date resume 2017 fall class schedule references Do Some Homework: do some research on the departments you are interested in and/or the types of jobs they are trying to fill RSC Open Positions Prepare an Elevator Pitch: an elevator pitch allows the job candidate to get their point across quickly. These pitches last for about 30 seconds and contain roughly 100 to 150 words. This last point is important because developing a good elevator pitch may take some practice. A good elevator pitch will tell the listener why you are a uniquely qualified applicant. It should also convey to the employer the benfits you will bring to their company. Finally, practicing the pitch will result in greater confidence, create the opportunity to improve the pitch, and allow the pitch to sound more natural. Sign Up for RSC Speed Interviews

title: RSC Human Resources
text: RSC Human Resources - RSC Employment Opportunities Contact Us Working at the Rhatigan Student Center (RSC) at Wichita State University is a unique and rewarding experience. As the central gathering place on campus, the RSC is a lively, student-focused environment where no two days are the same. Whether you’re helping organize campus events, assisting guests, or working in one of the many services like the Shocker Store or event spaces, you’re playing a key role in creating a welcoming and engaging atmosphere for the WSU community. The RSC is more than just a workplace - it’s a community. You'll have the chance to work alongside a team of students and staff, build valuable customer service and leadership skills, and grow both personally and professionally. The center’s commitment to excellence, inclusion, and student development means employees are supported and encouraged to succeed. Plus, with flexible scheduling, a central location on campus, and a variety of roles across different departments, the RSC offers convenience and a supportive environment that fits well with academic life. For students especially, it’s an ideal place to gain real-world experience while staying connected to the energy of campus life.

title: Sodance
text: Sodance - Policy Rhatigan Student Center Student Organization Dances Scheduled On The RSC East Patio, RSC Ballroom Or Room #223 Purpose The Rhatigan Student Center, in an attempt to provide the necessary safeguards which will contribute to a safe and successful event, wish to establish the following policies and procedures. Programming Certification Workshop Any student organization in good standing with Wichita State University Division of Student Affairs is eligible to sponsor student dances. The Division of Student Affairs will sponsor a Programming Certification Workshop for student organizations. Any member of a student organization who will be responsible for planning and hosting a dance on the East Patio, in the Ballroom or Room #223 must attend the workshop. Upon successful completion of the Programming Certification Workshop, those members are eligible to schedule a dance through the University Reservations Office, and are eligible to serve as the organization's on-site representative for events scheduled in the Rhatigan Student Center or its environs. Scheduling, Confirmation, Fee Payment Student organizations are encouraged to reserve the East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223 in the Rhatigan Student Center for events. Each organization is allowed two scheduled activities per month during the fall and spring semesters. No student dances will be scheduled during the summer session. A dance must be scheduled a minimum of two weeks prior to the event. Scheduling, confirmation, and fee payment are handled through the University Reservations Office located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, or by calling 978-3475. To confirm a reservation a deposit is required. The confirmation deposit will be applied towards the East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223 usage fees and charges. Contract and Fee Payment Schedule The signed event contract along with all applicable fees must be received by the Reservations Manager a minimum of five (5) working days prior to the scheduled event. Failure to meet the deadline will constitute cancellation of the event. Click Here to obtain a PDF of the contract Cancellation Procedures The confirmation deposit is refundable if a reservation is cancelled five (5) working days prior to the scheduled event. Any cancellation after five (5) working days up to twenty-four (24) hours prior to the scheduled event will constitute loss of deposit. Eligibility and Admittance Procedures for Student Dances The student organization will control admittance to student dances under the following guidelines and with supervision of the Rhatigan Student Center Event Manager. The following categories of persons with valid picture identification are eligible to attend a student dance. Category 1: A Wichita State University or other college student with a current student identification card. Category 2: A graduate/alumni with a graduate, alumni, or Greek ID. Category 3: Active members of the Armed Forces of the United States with a current military ID. To ensure the safety of students attending the dance everyone must produce a picture ID that establishes his/her eligibility to attend the dance. Each eligible person attending the dance may sponsor a guest, if the guest has a picture ID. An eligible person must accompany his/her guest to the event and register with the organization in charge. Eligible persons without a guest are not required to register. The sponsoring organization will check ID's throughout the event and must ensure all persons attending the event meet the established attendance criteria. The Reservations Manager and the sponsoring organization's representative will determine a location to check ID's and collect admission. The Rhatigan Student Center Event Manager will monitor activities throughout the evening. If a violation should occur, the Event Manager will inform the sponsoring organization, who in turn will be expected to resolve the problem. Security The Wichita State University Police Department will coordinate the hiring of security officers for the safety of all attendees during an event held on the East Patio, in the Ballroom or Room #223 in the Rhatigan Student Center. The number of security officers needed will be determined by the University Police Chief based upon the nature of the event. Officers hired for the event will assist in all medical emergencies, provide assistance to the Event Manager and sponsoring organization, as well as enforce policies and procedures of the Rhatigan Student Center and Wichita State University. The sponsoring organization will incur the costs for four (4) officers at dances where alcohol is served or three (3) officers at dances where alcohol is not served. Wichita State University will incur any further security costs in most cases, including additional officers as determined by the University Chief of Police. Magnetometers The student organization is responsible for providing ID checkers, ushers, and attendants for the East Patio, Ballroom and Room #223, as determined by the Reservations Manager. Loitering is prohibited on Rhatigan Student Center premises and in the parking lot. Dances will end no later than 1:00 A.M. The East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223, surrounding environs, and the parking lot must be vacated within thirty (30) minutes of the dance's scheduled ending time. Due to security reasons the student organization will not permit a person who leaves the Rhatigan Student Center East Patio, Ballroom or Room #223 to return to the dance. The sponsoring organization is responsible for handling and security of its funds. The sponsoring organization is responsible for controlling its members and guests during the event. Security officers will provide assistance as needed. All policies and procedures not covered herein will be covered by the Event Manager at an Event Briefing one hour prior to the event. Advertisement Advertisement of all events is encouraged, however, it is required that groups obtain approval from the Reservations Manager prior to advertising. The following information is required on all advertisements: Name of the sponsoring organization. Specifically state who is eligible to attend event. Identify the start and end times for the event. Food and Beverage/Alcoholic Beverage Service University Dining Services retains all rights to sell and/or serve food and beverages within Rhatigan Student Center facilities and its environs. Organizations requiring food and/or beverage service for an event must contract for the service through the University Dining Services' Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3477. Cereal malt beverage and/or alcoholic liquor service must be in compliance with University policy. Event Briefing The Rhatigan Student Center Event Manager will conduct a mandatory briefing one hour prior to the event's scheduled starting time, for representatives of the sponsoring organization and all security officers. Introductions, policies and procedures, and individual assignments will be made. We strongly suggest the sponsoring organization's faculty/graduate advisor be present as well. The sponsoring organization's certified representative who signed the contract and any persons assigned a duty such as ID checkers, ushers, attendants, and admission personnel are required to attend, NO exceptions. The event briefing will start at the University Reservations Office. If the required personnel from the sponsoring organization are not present the Event Manager is authorized to cancel the event. Ending Times The sponsoring organization will make an announcement fifteen minutes prior to the end of the event, advising all persons in attendance of the scheduled end time. Music will stop precisely at the scheduled end time. In order to ensure a safe and casual exit, thirty (30) minutes will be allowed for the exiting of the environs and parking lot. Policy and Procedure Violations The Reservations Manager or the Event Manager may cancel any event if the sponsoring organization fails to correct or comply with the Rhatigan Student Center Event Policy or fulfill its responsibilities either prior to or during the event. Any safety or security issue that may arise during an event which is not corrected on the spot can result in the immediate termination of the dance. Event policy violations can result in the suspension of the student organization's privilege to reserve the Rhatigan Student Center environs for further events. A Division of Student Affairs review panel hears and resolves all grievances. Liability The sponsoring organization will be held responsible for the actions of the persons attending the event regardless of whether those persons are members of their organization. The organization is responsible for any physical damage to the premises and/or equipment. Effective : 7/1994 Revised : 1/2003 (metal detectors) for security screening at events are available upon request from the Rhatigan Student Center. If used, security officers will operate the magnetometers.
reason: clear procedures for scheduling, organizing, and managing student dances with detailed policies and responsibilities

title: Postingnotices
text: Postingnotices - POLICY RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER POSTING OF NOTICES The bulletin board on the first floor across from the display cases and next to the E-mail station is the designated location in the Rhatigan Student Center for displaying posters and flyers. The bulletin board is divided into sections, with each section being designated for a specific subject. Each section is identified with a laminated sign at the top of the board. The sections are designated as follows: Community Information-displays notices of events or information of local interest. Classified-displays notices of items for sale or rent or to buy. Services-displays notices of information about services for hire (i.e. typing services, maid services, tutoring, etc.). Campus Organizations-displays notices about events, services or information sponsored by a campus organization. University Departments-displays notices about events, services or information sponsored by a University department. Postings are limited to one (1) flyer/poster per heading. The size of the postings are limited to no larger than 11" X 17". Groups should place the flyer/poster under the appropriate heading on the bulletin board. No flyers/posters shall be posted on the exterior of the Rhatigan Student Center. They may not be placed on painted surfaces, glass or vinyl walls anywhere on the interior or exterior walls of the Rhatigan Student Center or its surrounding environments. The bulletin board will be cleared of all flyers/posters on the last day of each month. The Rhatigan Student Center staff will have charge of removing flyers/posters monthly as well as any flyers/posters that do not comply with these guidelines. Commercial businesses may not use Rhatigan Student Center space for posting notices without prior approval from the University Reservations Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 316-978-3475. The Rhatigan Student Center will not accept the responsibility for any flyers/posters taken or removed from the bulletin board. Flyers/Posters or table tents may be placed in dining areas in the Rhatigan Student Center only with prior approval from the Director of University Dining Services and the Rhatigan Student Center's Marketing Manager. During Student Government Association elections, each candidate may post up to three (3) flyers/posters around the Rhatigan Student Center with string on brick walls only. Tape may not be used on any walls. Flyers/posters must be removed the day following the election. Permission for exceptions to any of the above policies must be requested in writing to the University Reservations Office. Effective: 1/2003

text: Foodguidestaff - Wichita State University Guidelines for University Departments, Faculty, Unclassified Professionals & Classified Staff to Dispense Food on Campus Definitions " Food " is any raw or processed substance or ingredients intended for consumption. " Perishable Food " is food capable of (1) supporting rapid and progressive growth of infectious or toxigenic microorganisms that may cause food infections or food intoxications, or (2) supporting the growth or toxin product of Clostridium botulinum. Perishable food is considered potentially hazardous. Complimentary Food/Closed Potluck Persons providing the Food must do so at their own expense. Persons eating the Food provided will not be charged. Food may not be offered to the general public for consumption or offered in a public setting. Perishable Food must be maintained at its required temperature. Hot food must be kept hot and cold food must be kept cold. Closed potluck events may include Perishable Food items. Copies of the "Guidelines for University Departments, Faculty, Unclassified Professionals and Classified Staff to Dispense Food on Campus" are on file in the office of the Vice President for Administration & Finance. Effective: 4/2002
reason: provides guidelines and definitions related to food handling on campus, useful for understanding university policies

title: Foodguidestudent
text: Foodguidestudent - Wichita State University Guidelines for Student Organizations to Sell/Dispense Food on Campus Definitions " Food " is any raw or processed substance or ingredients intended for consumption. " Certified Food Handler " is defined as any person working in a food preparation facility who engages in food preparation or who comes in contact with any food, utensil or equipment used in connection with preparation or service of food, and who has successfully completed food sanitation education program provided by the Kansas Health Department. " Perishable Food " is food capable of (1) supporting rapid and progressive growth of infectious or toxigenic microorganisms that may cause food infections or food intoxications, or (2) supporting the growth or toxin product of Clostridium botulinum. Perishable food is considered potentially hazardous. Permissible Food Service (Dispensing) Activities by Student Organizations Closed Potluck/Complimentary Food Sponsoring student organizations must obtain approval to provide closed Potluck/Complimentary Food prior to the scheduled event, from the administrator of the building where the event is to be held. All applicable building policies/procedures must be adhered to by sponsoring student organizations. Persons providing the Food must do so at their own expense. Persons eating the Food provided will not be charged. Food may not be offered to the general public for consumption. Perishable Food must be maintained at its required temperature. Hot Food must be kept hot and cold Food must be kept cold. Closed potluck events may include Perishable Food items. Failure to adhere to these guidelines by student organizations may result in loss of privileges, and/or disciplinary action instigated by the Vice President of Campus Life and University Relations. Permissible Food Service (Sales) Activities by Student Organizations Bake Sales Sponsoring student organizations must obtain approval to hold a bake sale prior to the scheduled sale, from the Office of Campus Life and University Relations as well as from the administrator of the building where the sale is to be held. All applicable building policies/procedures must be adhered to by sponsoring student organizations. A Certified Food Handler must supervise the preparation and distribution of bake sale items. All bake sale items must be bundled into individual servings and sealed in either plastic wrap or zip-lock bags. Non-sealing sandwich bags and aluminum foil is not sufficient. Approved signage must be located at the bake sale site identifying the sponsoring organization and indicating that the bake sale items were prepared under the supervision of a Certified Food Handler. Perishable Food may not be sold at a bake sale. Failure to adhere to these procedures by student organizations may result in loss of privileges, and/or disciplinary action instigated by the Vice President of Campus Life and University Relations. Perishable Food Sales Sponsoring student organizations must obtain approval to hold a perishable food sale prior to the scheduled sale date, from the Office of Campus Life and University Relations as well as from the administrator of the building where the sale is to be held. All applicable building policies/procedures must be adhered to by sponsoring student organizations. Certified Food Handler must be present during food preparation, distribution and sale of perishable food items. Perishable Food sales will be limited to specialty foods not otherwise available for sale or distribution on campus or foods deemed integral to the nature of the event. Approved signage must be located at the Perishable Food sale site perishable food items were prepared under the supervision of a Certified Food Handler. Failure to adhere to these procedures by student organizations may result in loss of privileges, and/or disciplinary action instigated by the Vice President of Campus Life and University Relations. Copies of the "Guidelines for Student Organizations to Sell/Dispense Food on Campus" are on file in the office of the Vice President for Office of Campus Life and University Relations. Effective: 4/2002
reason: clear procedures and rules for student organizations selling/dispensing food on campus

title: Banners
text: Banners - POLICY RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER BANNER HANGING Space for departments or organizations to hang banners on the outside of the Rhatigan Student Center may be scheduled through the University Reservations Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3475. The East Balcony is the designated area for hanging banners and is limited to three at a time. Banner sizes are limited to a maximum size of 4' X 15'. Banner space is available to SGA recognized organizations, Wichita State University departments or groups sponsored by either. Groups may reserve banner space for a maximum of two (2) weeks consecutively and must wait two (2) weeks between reservations. Groups are responsible for providing their banner along with 50' of rope that will withstand the various elements, to the University Reservations Office no less than two (2) days prior to the first day of the scheduled reservation. The RSC Operations staff will hang all banners and remove banners within two (2) days after the last day of the scheduled reservation. The University Reservations Office or the Rhatigan Student Center cannot assume any responsibility for damage while hanging or removing banners. If a banner is not picked up in the University Reservations Office by the sponsoring organization in a timely manner after the last day of the scheduled reservation, a fee may be assessed to the group for the Rhatigan Student Center to store and/or dispose of the banner. Banners cannot promote, advertise or otherwise advocate an illegal activity, or violate any Rhatigan Student Center or Wichita State University policies. All verbiage printed on the banner must be written in and/or translated to the English language, and must be approved by the University Reservations Office prior to the banner being displayed. The Rhatigan Student Center cannot accept responsibility for damages or theft of banners. Effective: 9/1998
reason: provides specific policy details for banner hanging at Rhatigan Student Center, useful for student organizations

title: Handbills
text: Handbills - POLICY WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY INFORMATION/HANDBILLS DISTRIBUTION The distribution of handbills shall be prohibited in those areas devoted primarily to instruction or study or at the immediate sites and times of enclosed public events. (1/77, amended 10/80) Handbills/information may be distributed by either a student organization or a political candidate in the Rhatigan Student Center providing the distribution is being expedited from behind a table. Handbills may not be passed out using the manner of approaching persons in the halls, lounges or restaurants. There is no charge to a student organization using a table for distributing information. A candidate who is not sponsored by a student organization however, will be charged the standard table rental. Tables may not be used for the purpose of selling political propaganda, or for any fundraising activities. Effective: 9/1998
reason: clear policy on handbill distribution with specific rules and exceptions

title: Loungeuse
text: Loungeuse - POLICY RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER LOUNGE USAGE Public lounges are located throughout the Rhatigan Student Center and are available for scheduling special events. Lounges may be reserved by Wichita State University departments and recognized student organizations at no charge. Groups who are not recognized may reserve the lounges for a rental fee. There are three (3) large lounges available for scheduling, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center. The Fireplace Lounge is located on the North end of the building, the Skylight Lounge at the Northeast, and the Shocker Lounge in the center of the building. Reservations for the Rhatigan Student Center lounges may be made through the University Reservations Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3475. The following guidelines apply: Reservations are made on a first-come, first-serve basis. A confirmation deposit may be required. The use of audio equipment is limited to one (1) public area at a time. A sound level agreeable to the Rhatigan Student Center, as determined by the University Reservations Office must be maintained. Furniture in the lounges may be moved only upon special request. Rhatigan Student Center personnel will be responsible for moving furniture according to any special requests. These requests should be made at the time the area is scheduled. Events in the Shocker lounge may not block entry into, nor exit from Commerce Bank or the Shocker Card Center. Cancelations should be made three (3) business days prior to the scheduled date. Effective: 7/1994
reason: clear student procedures for lounge reservations and usage guidelines

title: Alcohol
text: Alcohol - POLICY RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER CEREAL MALT BEVERAGE/ALCOHOLIC LIQUOR POLICIES CEREAL MALT BEVERAGE The Rhatigan Student Center holds a Cereal Malt Beverage (CMB) license only for the Rec Center. Customers wishing to serve 3.2% beer in any other area of the RSC must obtain a temporary license from the City of Wichita, by applying for one at City Hall Express, in the City building on North Main street. Once a group has obtained a CMB license, they must provide a copy of the license to University Dining Service for their records. When these steps have been completed, the following policies will be enforced: University Dining Services is in charge of checking individuals to insure all are of legal drinking age, and for providing & dispensing the 3.2% beer and collecting monies. No persons under 21 years of age are allowed to possess or to consume 3.2% beer at any event at which these beverages are served or sold. If an event is open to the public, the sponsoring group may not purchase 3.2% beer and then give it away to attendees. University Dining Service must make available, a non-alcoholic beverage at events where 3.2% beer is served. Consumption of 3.2% beer is permitted only within the approved area designated for the event. For events scheduled in the Rec Center, the sponsoring group must purchase the 3.2% beer from the Rec Center. It is the Rec Center's responsibility for checking individuals to insure all are of legal drinking age, and for providing & dispensing the 3.2% beer and collecting monies. ALCOHOLIC LIQUOR Board of Regents policy states that alcoholic liquor may be served only at luncheons, dinners or receptions which occur in connection with official university events and/or fund-raising activities for university programs. The service of alcoholic liquor at such events must be approved in advance by the President of the University, or the President's designee. The service of alcoholic liquor in circumstances other than above is prohibited unless approved by the University President, or the President's designee. Policies for serving alcoholic liquor in the Rhatigan Student Center are as follows: A letter of approval from the President or his designee must be provided to University Dining Service for their records. University Dining Service is responsible for dispensing all alcoholic liquor in the RSC. The sponsoring group must provide the alcoholic liquor to University Dining Service for serving. The sponsoring group must purchase the setups, bartender service, etc. from University Dining Service. At all events in which alcoholic liquor is approved for use, a non-alcoholic beverage must also be made available to attendees. Food must be made available at all functions where alcoholic liquor is served. Alcoholic liquor may not be served at an event that is open to the public. Alcoholic liquor may not be sold to attendees of an event. Alcoholic liquor may not be served to persons under the age of 21. Effective: 9/1998
reason: clear alcohol policies with step-by-step instructions for obtaining licenses and serving guidelines

title: Campusfacilities
text: Campusfacilities - POLICY WICHITA STATE UNIVERSITY USE OF CAMPUS FACILITIES To carry out the University's mission, the facilities of Wichita State University are primarily for use by its students, faculty and staff for activities and programs that are directly related to the basic educational functions of teaching, research, and preparation of scholarly material. University facilities shall be made available on a basis that attempts to ensure fair and appropriate usage thereof while accommodating the University's academic and instructional needs and protecting the investment of the State in said facilities. Classrooms, laboratories and other facilities which are to be used for teaching and instructional programs are scheduled by the Registrar on the basis of need and as a first priority. After the initial academic schedules are reviewed and assigned space, unscheduled space is made available to the University Reservations Office for assignment to qualified users as a second priority on a first-request basis. All use of University facilities for purposes other than teaching and instructional programs, whether sponsored by individual schools, colleges or departments of the University; by bureaus, centers or institutes of the University; or by officially recognized organizations must be scheduled by the University Reservations Office located in the Rhatigan Student Center or the person designated to make reservations of the Special Use Facilities listed on the reverse side. As a third priority, the University, as a State institution with a basic service function, may grant use of its facilities to: University, State of Kansas, and other Governmental Agencies, etc. Non-University businesses, churches, groups, agencies, etc. General Campus Facilities The first priority for use of University facilities is assigned to colleges, schools, departments, bureaus, agencies and sponsored organizations or activities in carrying out the University's basic educational functions enumerated above. The general public may be invited to attend activities sponsored by the University through its colleges, schools, departments, bureaus and agencies or by a sponsored University organization. Colleges, schools, departments, bureaus and agencies and University-sponsored organizations should limit the sponsorship of non-academic activities to programs which fall under the purview of their official departmental function.
reason: clear policy on facility usage with prioritization and reservation procedures

title: Overview
text: Overview - The Rhatigan Student Center Facility Policies and Procedures Facilities and services of the Rhatigan Student Center are open to the University and general public, subject to Wichita State University and Rhatigan Student Center policies and procedures. Reservations are accepted between 7:30 AM-5 PM, Monday through Friday. A reservation may be made in person in the University Reservations Office, located on the first floor in the Rhatigan Student Center, by calling 316-978-3475 or by e-mailing the University Reservations Office at LetsMeet@wichita.edu . E-mail or telephone requests submitted on a holiday or a Saturday or Sunday, will not be processed until the next business day. Meeting room reservations should be made at least 48 hours in advance. More time should be allowed for catered events, preferably a minimum of two weeks prior to the date of the event. Requests are taken on a first come, first serve basis. Room assignments are made according to the size and function of the event. The Facility Policies and Procedures are designed to give facility users a clear understanding of their responsibilities. EVENT LOGISTICS Access and Event Times Facility access and use must be within allotted confirmed times as noted on the Event Confirmation. Confirmed times must include event preparation, decorating, and/or rehearsal times as well as time after the event to remove decorations, user's equipment and other items. Events that have not removed all decorations, equipment and other items by the scheduled ending time for the event, will be assessed an After-Hours fee. The Rhatigan Student Center staff shall have the right to access and enter the event space for any reasonable purpose during the confirmed time. Cancelation by Facility Permission to use the Rhatigan Student Center is granted subject to observance of regulations. The Rhatigan Student Center may revoke this permission immediately upon failure to timely comply with pre-event requirements/deadlines, for any violation of use conditions or regulations, or at any time for misrepresentation. The Rhatigan Student Center may terminate any part of this permission without notice in the event of an emergency situation that, in the opinion of the Rhatigan Student Center, would make the event unfeasible. Cancelation by User Groups are responsible for all rental fees, when applicable, if their reservation in the Rhatigan Student Center is canceled less than 24 hours prior to the date of the event. For recurring events, the first time a group is a "no show", a warning will be made with the group's contact person. A second "no show" within the same semester will result in the group's scheduling privileges being suspended for the remainder of that semester. Cancelations for catered events (at 316-978-5863) are to be made no less than 5 business days prior to the event, in order to avoid incurring a cancellation charge. To receive a refund of a confirmation deposit, notice must be received in the University Reservations Office and acknowledged, no less than ten (10) working days prior to the date of the event. Eligibility University departments and recognized student organizations receive priority when requesting space in the Rhatigan Student Center, subject to Wichita State University and Rhatigan Student Center policies and procedures. Student organizations who have not been recognized by the Student Government Association but are in the process of getting recognized, are entitled to two organizational meetings at no charge, prior to its recognition. The purpose of these organizational meetings is to announce the group's establishment to the University's student population in order to recruit new members. Event Schedules Daily Event Schedules are posted at all entrances into the Rhatigan Student Center as well as outside of each meeting room. Facilities Users of the Rhatigan Student Center shall observe all applicable Rhatigan Student Center and Wichita State University policies, as well as all local, state and federal laws, statutes, and ordinances. The user shall only have the use of the facilities as stated in the Event Confirmation. All alterations to the facility, building systems or equipment are subject to approval from the University Reservations Office. The user shall follow all reasonable directives from Rhatigan Student Center staff. At the end of the event, the facility should be left in a clean, safe condition. Inclement Weather Sites Consideration should be given for events scheduled to take place outdoors, regarding an alternative indoor location to hold the event, in the case of inclement weather. Inclement weather sites will not be scheduled for events where control of room capacity and banned items (donated food, alcohol, etc.) cannot be maintained. Insurance Depending on the nature and scope of the facility use, the user may be required to furnish a certificate of insurance naming the Rhatigan Student Center and various University entities as additionally insured. Required certificates must be received by the Rhatigan Student Center fourteen (14) days prior to the event date. Liability Users of the Rhatigan Student Center agree to indemnify, protect, defend and hold harmless the Rhatigan Student Center, Wichita State University, its Board of Trustees, officers, employees, agents and students from and against any and all claims, demands, losses, costs, damages or liability of any nature or character arising out of or by reason of the execution or performance of the rights, duties and obligations arising out of or incidental to the use of the facility or equipment. The user agrees to abide and enforce the rules, regulations and policies governing the facility as set forth by the Rhatigan Student Center and Wichita State University. The user accepts all responsibility for any damages to premises, equipment or grounds resulting from use of the facility. Premises The Rhatigan Student Center may use any part of the premises that is not confirmed to a user at any time, providing that such does not interfere with the user's use of confirmed space. Priority University departments as well as registered/recognized student organizations are given priority for usage of the Rhatigan Student Center. Off-campus groups and individuals have scheduling privileges of the facilities after campus needs are met. Reassignment of Facilities Should space in the Rhatigan Student Center become unavailable due to an emergency, the Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to reassign the user to another space within the facility or reschedule for another date. The University Reservations Office will notify the user as soon as the need arises for a reassignment of facilities. Reoccurring Events Weekly meetings may be scheduled one semester at a time, beginning in July or December. Monthly or quarterly meetings may be scheduled for the upcoming academic year, beginning in July. The University Reservations Office reserves the right to make room changes in order to accommodate special events. Responsible Party(s)/Event Coordination Deadline The person(s) who schedules the facility shall be the responsible party. If the person coordinating the event is not planning to be in attendance the day of the event, a designated representative will be communicated to the University Reservations Office. This representative shall take all reasonable actions to assure event safety, to prevent damage to the facility and equipment, and to see that these conditions and other policies and regulations outlined in the Facility Policies and Procedures are met. Special Requirements Special requirements, such as overnight storage of equipment, activation of data/phone lines or signals, access for news/media, or other such requirements must be coordinated in advance with the respective University departments. Charges for such services could apply. FEES, PAYMENTS AND TAXES After-Hours Fees University departments, individuals and off-campus users desiring use of the Rhatigan Student Center at times other than during its regular hours of operation, may be charged an after-hours fee. Current after-hours fees may be verified with the University Reservations Office. Deposits/Payment If applicable, a deposit may be required in order to confirm a reservation. Facilities will not be held beyond ten (10) working days without receipt of this deposit. If the requested date is more than three (3) months in advance, a 50% deposit of the estimated costs is required to confirm the reservation. The balance of the estimated costs is due ten (10) working days in advance of the scheduled date. If the requested date is less than ten (10) working days in advance, the total of the estimated costs is required to confirm the reservation. After final payment has been received, any charges incurred due to last minute changes, must be paid at the time the changes are requested. Outstanding Balances The University Reservations Office invoices weekly. All invoices must be paid within thirty (30) days of the event date. Accounts must be paid in full in order for a University department or student organization to be allowed to maintain scheduling privileges. Permits and Taxes The scheduling organization is responsible for obtaining permits or licenses as required by law. A copy of such permits or licenses must be provided to the University Reservations Office five (5) working days prior to the scheduled event date. EQUIPMENT AND PROPERTY Abandoned Property Any property not removed from the Rhatigan Student Center that has not been claimed within forty-eight (48) hours following the conclusion of the scheduled event will be considered abandoned by the user and/or its exhibitors. The Rhatigan Student Center may take possession of it and treat it as its own or dispose of such property without liability. The user may be liable for the costs incurred in disposing of the abandoned property. Damage to Facility/Damage Deposits Users of the Rhatigan Student Center are responsible for the condition of the facility for the duration of their scheduled event. The Rhatigan Student Center shall inspect the facility to determine if any damage was sustained as a result of the user's occupancy. Repairs for significant damages will be charged to the user. Some events/organizations may require refundable damage deposits. Decorations/Signs The University Reservations Office must approve any decorations, banners or signs. Rhatigan Student Center signage cannot be covered or otherwise obstructed. Nothing may be affixed to the drapes, vinyl coverings, ceilings, wood surfaces, painted walls or floors. All decorations must be flame retardant. All decorations, props and outdoor/indoor directional and promotional signage must be removed by the user immediately following the event or they will be disposed of by the Rhatigan Student Center staff. Rice, birdseed, glitter, confetti or substances that stain or become imbedded into the carpet are not allowed in the Rhatigan Student Center. Equipment All Rhatigan Student Center equipment (i.e. tables, chairs, staging, flip charts, etc.) will be set up by the Rhatigan Student Center staff. The user will be responsible for all Rhatigan Student Center owned equipment and will be held liable for the equipment if lost, stolen, damaged or misplaced. Special Equipment Users of the Rhatigan Student Center intending to bring any equipment into the Rhatigan Student Center that requires access to facility water, high voltage electrical, satellite signals or such systems must receive advance authorization and approval from the University Reservations Office. User's Property Users of the Rhatigan Student Center assume full responsibility to safeguard all materials, goods or property owned or used by the user or any of its exhibitors or guests. Users hereby waive any claims against the Rhatigan Student Center and its employees for damages to, theft or loss of property. SAFETY ISSUES Capacities The Rhatigan Student Center will not permit its facilities to be occupied greater than the listed capacities. Emergency Medical Service The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to require emergency medical services be present, if deemed necessary, based on the type of event scheduled. Flames/Fire Open flames and the burning of any materials, including incense, is prohibited. Use of candles must receive advance approval from the University Reservations Office and meet fire code regulations. Fire Regulations Users, exhibitors and their guests of the Rhatigan Student Center must comply with all Federal, State and local fire and building codes that apply to spaces of public assembly. Facility fire fighting and emergency equipment may not be hidden or obstructed. All emergency exits, hallways and aisles leading from the Rhatigan Student Center must be kept clear and unobstructed. Recreational Devices Bicycles, skates and other such recreational devices are not allowed to be operated in or around the Rhatigan Student Center. Security - The Rhatigan Student Center staff and/or the WSU Police shall solely determine and control security arrangements including but not limited to the type and number of security personnel and placement and use of security personnel. The Rhatigan Student Center staff and/or the WSU Police reserve the right to require police at events where alcohol beverages are served. Only WSU Police or their designees may be hired to act as security for events scheduled in the Rhatigan Student Center. Only licensed law enforcement officers may carry firearms in the facility. Smoking - The Rhatigan Student Center is a non-smoking facility. Special Effects Fog machines, dry ice or smoke machines that may trigger the fire protection system to be activated or impede an evacuation from the facility, are not permitted in the Rhatigan Student Center. Weapons/Firearms All weapons and firearms are strictly prohibited in the Rhatigan Student Center. MISCELLANEOUS Alcohol Service Users of the Rhatigan Student Center agree to abide by and to enforce the University policies regarding the consumption of alcoholic beverages. All alcoholic beverage service arrangements for events in the Rhatigan Student Center must be coordinated through WSU Dining Services. Animals Animals are prohibited in the Rhatigan Student Center with the exception of service animals assisting persons with special needs. Conduct Users and guests of the Rhatigan Student Center shall not interfere with the regular use of the Rhatigan Student Center by the public or other facility guests. Excessive noise or other disruptive behavior is prohibited. The Rhatigan Student Center may remove any person whom they believe is disrupting or obstructing the daily operation and management of the facility. Users who abuse their usage of the facility will be denied future scheduling privileges. Food and Beverage Service WSU Dining Services is the exclusive vendor of all food and beverage services in the Rhatigan Student Center. Copies of the Food Guidelines-University Departments and Food Guidelines-Student Organizations may be obtained from the University Reservations Office for reference. Gambling Users of the Rhatigan Student Center agree to abide by and enforce the University policies regarding gambling in the facility. Publicity The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to approve, in advance, all forms of advertising or publicity for any activity scheduled in its facility. Users shall not advertise any event until a confirmed reservation has been made. Vehicle Parking/Unloading Users and guests of the Rhatigan Student Center must abide by all University parking/traffic requirements, including but not limited to passenger and equipment loading/unloading regulations, observance of authorized parking locations, payment of fees, and display of vehicle parking permits. Access to the loading docks must be coordinated with the University Reservations Office prior to the event. Parking in the loading docks is prohibited and violators will be ticketed and/or towed at the owner's expense. ADDITIONAL POLICIES Additional policies for the Rhatigan Student Center may be found in their entirety, on the Rhatigan Student Center's website at www.wichita.edu /rsc . They are listed under Policies and Procedures: Banner Hanging Credit Card Solicitation Food & Beverage Service Guidelines for Student Organizations to Sell/Dispense Food on Campus Guidelines for University Departments, Faculty, Unclassified Professionals and Classified Staff to Dispense Food on Campus Lost & Found Patio Usage Plastic Table Tents Posting of Notices Serving Cereal Malt Beverage/Alcohol Student Organization Events Scheduled on the East Patio, RSC Ballroom or Room #223 Student Organization Events Scheduled in the CAC Theater Table Usage/Merchandise Sales Tent Usage Usage of Facility Beyond Scheduled Building Hours
reason: clear procedures and policies for facility use, reservations, and event logistics

title: Tableuse
text: Tableuse - POLICY RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER TABLE USAGE/MERCHANDISE SALES Tables available for distributing information and/or merchandise sales in the Rhatigan Student Center are reserved through the University Reservations Office, located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center, 978-3475. The following guidelines apply: RESERVATIONS Tables available for scheduling are located on the first floor of the Rhatigan Student Center. There are four (4) stationary locations which are reserved on a first-come, first-serve basis. A 30" X 72" table and two (2) chairs are provided. Groups are not allowed to provide additional tables or equipment at the locations. There is no rental charge for table usage to SGA recognized organizations, Wichita State University departments or groups sponsored by either. Groups who are not recognized or sponsored will be charged a daily rental fee. This fee must be paid by cash, certified check or money order ten (10) business days prior to the scheduled date. Failure to meet the deadline will constitute an automatic cancellation of the event. Cancellations must be made ten (10) business days prior to the scheduled date. Any cancellation made after ten (10) days will constitute a loss in rental fees previously paid, or a charge assessed to the scheduling party. Signage may be hung from the tables with masking tape only. Nothing may be affixed to brick, vinyl, glass or painted walls with tape, nails or thumbtacks. Signage may be hung with string on the brick walls only. A maximum of two (2) signs may be used. A person affiliated with the sponsoring organization must be at the table at all times in order that they may answer questions, etc. These persons must stay within the proximity of the table. Hawking, defined as "advertising or peddling by shouting", is not permitted. All items must be removed from the table by the sponsoring organization at the end of each day. Cleaning up of the area is the responsibility of the sponsoring organization. Groups reserving table space must identify the table as being sponsored by their organization. A sign for the table must be provided by the organization. Groups wishing to use any type of electronic equipment must have approval of the University Reservations Office prior to its use. In the event that extension cords are needed, groups are responsible for providing their own, subject to approval by the University Reservations Office. Secured facilities for items to be stored overnight are available upon request, at an additional charge. However, the Rhatigan Student Center cannot be held liable for the damages to or loss of such items due to accidents, riots, acts of God or other legitimate conditions beyond its control. MERCHANDISE SALES The sponsoring organization agrees to display or make available, all refund and guarantee policies. The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to schedule sales of similar or like items on the same day. The sponsoring organization is responsible for all loading and unloading of products to be sold. The Rhatigan Student Center cannot provide assistance. Carts/dollies are not available. Certain types of promotional activities/merchandise sales are not allowed in the Rhatigan Student Center. They include, but are not limited to: Food sales of any kind. Sales of items with copyrighted University logos. Sales that require people to pay in advance and receive their merchandise at a later date. Services and/or sales of items that conflict with services and/or items already being provided and/or sold by the Rhatigan Student Center, Wichita State University and/University Dining Services. Any items given away by the sponsoring organization must not conflict with items sold or given away by the Rhatigan Student Center. Approval of items may be obtained through the University Reservations Office. Certain items to be given away may be available through the University Bookstore or University Dining Services for purchase by the sponsoring organization. Sponsoring organizations who are soliciting credit card applications must obtain approval from the University Reservations Office for the types of credit cards to be promoted. Credit card solicitations may not occur beginning one week prior to the start of each semester, through the end of the 2 nd week of the semester. Any deviation from the above policies must be approved by the University Reservations Office. Requests for exceptions should be submitted in writing to the Reservations Manager. The Rhatigan Student Center and/or Wichita State University are not responsible for lost, stolen or damaged personal property or merchandise. In consideration for use of the Rhatigan Student Center facilities, the group waives any claim for damages or injury which may arise. Effective: 4/1997 Revised: 1/2003
reason: clear student procedures for table usage and merchandise sales with specific rules and deadlines

title: Beyondbldghours
text: Beyondbldghours - POLICY RHATIGAN STUDENT CENTER USAGE OF FACILITY BEYOND SCHEDULED BUILDING HOURS The Rhatigan Student Center has established operating hours for each fall and spring semester and each summer session. title: Catering Guidelines
text: Catering Guidelines - Catering Guidelines Application and Approval The Rhatigan Student Center allows flexible catering options for campus events. For additional information contact the RSC Event Services office at 316-978-3475 or letsmeet@wichita.edu Applications are available on the Rhatigan Student Center Event Services web page at http://www.wichita.edu/ESpolicies and can be filled out online or mailed in. Include a Certificate of Liability insurance naming Wichita State University Union Corporation as additional named insured. When we have received your application, it will be reviewed and within approximately 10 days you will receive email notification as to whether it has been approved. Wichita State University has an exclusive beverage contract with Coca Cola. All drinks served at WSU must be Coca Cola products. General Guidelines Catering must be provided by an approved caterer. All catering requests should accompany an existing space reservation. If your client has not already made a space reservation, please encourage them to contact their event coordinator or department office as soon as possible. At the Rhatigan Student Center, caterers may unload at either the west dock located off of Isley Lane or the south dock located near the parking garage. A service elevator is available near each loading dock to access meeting spaces on the second and third floor. Caterers may set up 2 hours in advance of the event start time. If you need additional time please contact your Event Coordinator. You must clean up immediately following your event. The Rhatigan Student Center may charge a $25 clean-up fee if facilities are not left in their original condition. The Rhatigan Student Center offers a prep kitchen on the third floor. Please note, we do not have kitchen facilities for cooking . All food must be prepared in advance. The Rhatigan Student Center will supply table and chairs, however, caterers must supply all tablecloths, napkins, glassware, serving ware and any items needed for catering your event. The Rhatigan Student Center will charge caterers a 10 percent commission on food sales at the Rhatigan Student Center. This commission is for food sales only and does not include beverages. Alcohol Service Guidelines Alcohol can be served in the Rhatigan Student Center by licensed providers. Caterers should be familiar with Wichita State University policy 11.07 available at http://webs.wichita.edu/inaudit/ch11_07.htm Please notify us if you are licensed to serve alcohol in the state of Kansas. There is an approval process. Your client must complete an alcohol request form and submit it 10 business days in advance with a certificate of insurance naming Wichita State University Union Corporation as named insured. All requests for alcohol service must be approved through the Wichita State University General Council's office.
reason: provides detailed guidelines and procedures for catering events at the Rhatigan Student Center

title: Rental Space Guidelines | Rhatigan Student Center | Wichita State University
text: Rental Space Guidelines | Rhatigan Student Center | Wichita State University - Rental Space Guidelines Please note that the information contained herein are the general guidelines and requirements included on most facility rental agreements we execute. Each individual event/booking shall have a specific agreement drawn up that will reflect the elements and requirements for each unique event. Event Coordinator Details The RSC Event Services will assist you in making your event possible at the Rhatigan Student Center. If you need assistance during your event, please contact any of the following numbers below: RSC Event Services: (316) 978-3475 (between 7:30 a.m.-5 p.m.,Monday-Friday) RSC Building Manager: (316) 978-3028 University Dining Services (Chartwells): (316) 978-3477 WSU Police Department: (316) 978-3450 Please look over your confirmation details for any mistakes or changes that need to be made and contact RSC Event Services at your earliest convenience. Contact Person The primary contact (Guest) will provide RSC Event Services with the name, email address, and phone number of the Guest's representative. The representative will be the sole person authorized to make changes to the event reservation. Rental Fees Please see the individual spaces chart for the rates of each room or location. Your rental fee includes the time allotted at the beginning and the end of the event for set ups and clean up. If you would like to decorate the day before, your event rooms will be billed at half the room rental rate. Event Times All reservations made through RSC Event Services include additional setup time before and after your event. Please note, that if additional time (over operating hours set by RSC Event Services) is needed, there will be additional incurred charges. Any events exceeding scheduled hours will be billed at $100 per hour. Event Details/Set Ups Set up notes for room reservations must be provided to your event coordinator at a minimum of one (1) month in advance. Receiving your set up notes in a timely manner will allow us the opportunity to coordinate our services in preparation for your event. Services Provided All rentals include set up of tables, chairs, audio/visual equipment, staging, and coat racks where requested. The Rhatigan Student Center has portable bars for drink service available for an additional fee. Cancellations, Changes, and Rescheduling The Rhatigan Student Center will make every effort to assist you with changes and rescheduling of your event. Please be advised that in the event your wedding has been canceled, any fees paid in advance will be refunded. However, your security deposit is non-refundable. Security The Rhatigan Student Center requires the presence of a Wichita State University police officer at all weddings. The cost of contracting a WSU police officer is included in your rental agreement. Insurance Clients must purchase liability insurance for events scheduled in the Rhatigan Student Center. A Certificate of Insurance provides proof to a third party that an individual has adequate insurance coverage. An "Additional Named Insured" does not give access to your insurance policy, but reduces liability. Please have your insurance company add the following information under Additional Named Insured: Wichita State University and Wichita State University Union Corporation You may contact your insurance company for a certificate of liability. Decorations You may decorate prior to your event. The Rhatigan Student Center allots a certain amount of time for preparations prior to and after the event has ended. If you need additional time to decorate, please contact your event coordinator for available times and any charges that may be incurred. The Rhatigan Student Center encourages decorations; however, please note the following: In accordance with state fire code, open candles are prohibited The use of glitter is prohibited Nothing is to be tacked, pinned, nailed, glued, or taped on any surface or walls of the venue Do not hang decorations from the ceiling Tables and chairs will be provided with your rental. The Beggs Ballroom is equipped with a sound system; however, it is not designed to play music effectively. If you choose to have music at your event, please contact a DJ of your choice who will be able to provide the appropriate equipment. Cleaning All guests will be responsible for returning the space to its original condition when an event is completed. Any decorations and equipment belonging to the guest or to a vendor associated with the event must be removed immediately following the event. The Rhatigan Student Center is not responsible for lost items and will not be able to provide additional storage space, outside of the packages you have chosen. Although housekeeping costs are included in your rental, please be aware that any additional clean-up services required during or following your event may be incurred. Parking During the fall and spring semesters, Wichita State's main campus is a permit-only parking environment on weekdays when the university is open for business. Visitors to the university may park without a permit for three (3) calendar days during each semester. Visitors may park in lots marked with prominent "V" signage. Please avoid parking in red parking lots. Parking in our Parking Garage by the Rhatigan Student Center is available at an hourly rate. Levels 2, 3, 4 and second and third ramps are hourly parking at $1.50 per hour. Ground level and first ramp is reserved. The parking garage is enforced 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Your event coordinator can provide you with an access code for the RSC Parking Garage. The access code will allow your guests to park at no cost to them. Following your event, you will be billed at $1.50 per hour for guests who utilized the RSC Parking Garage. Parking lots on the the perimeter of the campus are available for large events that require additional space. You can work with your event coordinator to request reserved parking. Damages In the event that there are damages to the Rhatigan Student Center's property or equipment by a guest or patron, the cost of the repair and replacing the damaged property may be charged to the client. Audio/Visual Equipment The Beggs Ballroom in the Rhatigan Student Center is equipped with audio/visual capability; however, the equipment is designed for presentation purposes. Guests interested in playing music for their event should contact a DJ to provide the appropriate equipment. Any audio/visual equipment provided by the Rhatigan Student Center should be left in the room and will be picked up by a Building Manager following your event. Catering/Dining Services University Dining Services (or Chartwells) is the premier dining services partner at Wichita State University. Chartwells is a full-service caterer and provides a wide variety menu of options including boxed lunches, hor d'oeuvres, buffets plated dinners, desserts, linens, china service, floral, and bartending service. You can contact Chartwells at (316) 978-3477. The university also offers flexible catering options to assist you with designing the perfect menu for your event. You may bring in an external caterer from our list of approved caterers , which continues to be updated frequently. If you plan to use a catering company that is not on our approved catering list, then you can encourage them to submit an Approved Caterer Application form prior to your event. This form will allow them to be part of our approved caterers to serve food on Wichita State University's premises. Learn more about our catering options. Note: Customers choosing an off-campus caterer for their event must have all food service containers and disposable items removed immediately following their event. Failure to clean up after the event will result in a service charge for cleaning. Alcohol Service Under Wichita State University's Policies and Procedures 11.07 / Sale, Service, And Consumption Of Alcohol On University Premises , requests for alcohol service must be approved by the WSU General Counsel prior to the date of the event. The service of alcohol without prior approval is prohibited. Approval is obtained by completing the following instructions at least 2-3 weeks in advance: Notify your event coordinator of your request Complete and submit the Alcohol Request form Off-campus guests must provide proof of liability insurance at the time the request is submitted Note: Alcohol service requires a licensed bartender and that bartender must be present throughout the event. Click here for a list of approved caterers offering alcohol service. Grace Memorial Chapel Please see your event coordinator for details on the use of the Grace Memorial Chapel. Book at the Rhatigan Student Center Ready for a tour? Contact us to schedule a tour and see the exquisite Shirley Beggs Ballroom that could make your wedding day unforgettable. Wedding Packages Contact Us

title: Catering Guidelines
text: Catering Guidelines - Forms If you have questions about these forms or policies, please call (316) 978-3475, email letsmeet@wichita.edu or visit Rhatigan Student Center Room 234. Approved Caterer Application — Submit this application to become a RSC approved caterer. Sponsorship Agreement — Submit this form to provide WSU departmental sponsorship of a non-WSU group usage of facilities. University Alcohol Service Request Form - Submit this application to request alcohol or cereal malt beverage service on campus. Policies RENTAL FEES Any room charges must be paid 2 weeks in advance. If no payment is made, the event will be cancelled. EVENT TIMES All reservations made through the Event Services office include additional set up time before and after an event. Please note, that if additional time (over those set by Event Services) is needed there may be an added charge. EVENT DETAILS / SET UPS Set-up notes for room reservations in the RSC or CAC Theater must be provided to the Event Services staff 2 weeks in advance of your events. Receiving your set up notes in a timely manner will allow us the opportunity to coordinate our services in preparation for your event. Note: Last-minute changes to your set-up (on the day of your event) may result in an additional charge of up to $100. CANCELLATIONS / NO SHOWS Guests who fail to cancel their reserved space and do not show up for their event will receive a warning letter and may be billed for set-up charges. Student organizations will have warning letters sent to Student Engagement and Belonging (SEB) and the organization’s advisor. If this occurs more than 2 times in a semester the group will lose its privilege to use Rhatigan Student Center facilities for the remainder of the semester. The Rhatigan Student Center reserves the right to change and/or cancel a reservation or alter the use of other assigned space with the understanding that, at all times, every effort shall be made to provide comparable facilities. PARKING Parking for events held at the RSC is available on the 2nd and 3rd floor of the parking garage located directly beside the RSC. Parking in the Parking Garage is $1.50 per hour. Parking lots on the perimeter of the campus can be reserved for large events that require additional space. Contact your Event Coordinator to request reserved parking. Validation codes for parking are available on request. Contact your Event Coordinator for additional information. DAMAGES In the event that damage to RSC property or equipment occurs by an RSC guest, its employees, agents, patrons or additional guests, the cost of repair and replacing the damaged property may be charged to the guest. title: Our History
text: Our History - From tragedy, a stronger future The Shocker Neighborhood Coalition was birthed in May of 2015 through a grant from the Kansas Health Foundation to work with Fairmount Neighborhood Association in response to a tragedy in Fairmount Park. The original initiative was Led by Mark Glaser, the university’s Public Policy and Management Center and included an in-depth survey of Fairmount residents which successfully defined community concerns and the community’s dedication to addressing them. Then Community liaison Darryl Carrington worked alongside community members to develop an identity for the neighborhood to rally around. As a result of this work, a greater understanding of the neighborhood was gained and the inter-sector economic development network tailored to the concerns of residents, called the Shocker Neighborhood Coalition. The three part series of reports can be found here . While the focus of early reporting and work centered on Fairmount Neighborhood, there was always a plan for the coalition to strengthen both the identity of a larger geographic area and economic sustainability of the same.

title: Shocker Neighborhood Commitment
text: Shocker Neighborhood Commitment - Wichita State’s Shocker Neighborhood Commitment extends the university's support to Future Shockers growing up in the neighborhoods that encircle the campus. A Shocker Promise to our neighbors Wichita State is proud to offer academic, financial and career resources and support for students who reside within the Shocker Neighborhood Coalition boundaries. Academic Support WSU offers a wide-ranging slate of college access programs that lead to academic success and student well-being. Shocker Promise The new Shocker Promise scholarship provides last-dollar funding to make college more attainable for Shocker Neighborhood students. Career/Workforce Readiness WSU's Career Accelerator matches students with employers and offers tons of resources to make you more marketable Eligibility To be eligible for participation in the Shocker Neighborhood Commitment, students must: Be a U.S. citizen or eligible noncitizen. Be a Sedgwick County, Kansas resident living in the Shocker Neighborhood (Oliver Road to I-135 and Central Avenue to K-96) at the time of application to Wichita State University. Be eligible for the Federal Pell Grant* Annual family income of $50,000 or less Be admitted for fall as a first-time freshman by February 1 of the applicant's senior year of high school. Submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) by March 1 of the applicant's senior year of high school for priority consideration. Minimum 2.5 high school GPA. Enroll full-time (complete 24-30 hours each academic year in the fall/spring/summer semesters) in a baccalaureate degree program. *Students must have financial need, and priority consideration will be given to students who are Pell Grant eligible. Family income information will be determined from the FAFSA. Students must have graduated high school within 9 months of initial enrollment as a first-time freshman. Students must meet the above criteria at the time of admission. The Shocker Promise Scholarship is a last payee scholarship to fill the gap of tuition and fees. Funding is limited and will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis to those who meet all requirements. If selected as a recipient, smaller previously awarded WSU freshmen scholarships will be replaced with the Shocker Promise. The Shocker Promise is a 4-year, last-payee scholarship designed to cover remaining costs associated with your tuition and fees and after applying all other gift aid, including waivers, scholarships and grants. How to get started! Apply to Wichita State If you're ready to build your ideal future, Wichita State has the unmatched resources, experiences and connections to make it happen. Apply and be admitted to Wichita State by February 1 of the applicant's senior year of high school. You may also qualify for an application fee waiver. Contact the Office of Undergraduate Admissions for details. Undergraduate Graduate Fill out the FAFSA Submit your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) by March 1 of the applicant's senior year of high school to apply for financial aid like work-study, grants, and loans. Wichita State's school code is 001950. Learn More
