title: Carrie Wyatt
text: Carrie Wyatt - Carrie Wyatt Student Support Specialist, Marketing and Communications, and Chair of CSD Student Affairs Communication and Sciences Disorders College of Health Professions I am honored to join in celebrating the accomplishments of Mrs. Carrie Wyatt as she is recognized as one of Wichita State University’s Bender of Twigs Honorees. Over the years, she has been a wonderful colleague, a Department advocate, and a smiling face to our students. I have known Carrie as a colleague since August 2009 when she joined the Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD). Before then she was with WSU’s Community Engagement Institute (CEI, formerly the Center for Community Support and Research). Prior to her work at CEI, she served in the role of the Dean’s Assistant and Scholarship Coordinator for the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Science (LAS). We are so glad that she moved to the College of Health Professions (CHP). When she joined CSD in August 2009, Carrie started as the Senior Administrative Specialist and the Website and Social Media Coordinator. In these roles she provided administrative support to faculty and students, and began coordinating strategic communications between CSD, CHP, and WSU’s Strategic Communications. In Spring 2017, she transitioned to the role of Academic Records Data Manager. This position continued her duties from the previous roles with additional duties relating to schedule building every semester across our four programs, admissions support for our two clinical graduate programs (MA-CSD [Speech-Language Pathology] and AuD [Doctor of Audiology]), undergraduate student program tracking and archiving, and accreditation support (e.g., tracking graduate students’ national certification testing results). During the post-COVID period when communication with the general public was crucial, Carrie took on additional roles with student outreach and Departmental online development. Carrie and I have worked together for several years on those aspects of every Department that require much time and attention to detail, including schedule building, faculty and student recognition, and Department event planning. In all these endeavors, she has supported the Department positively and effectively. As important as all those things are, there is something even more important on which she has always focused: supporting students in all aspects of student life. For example, she has been available to the students in our Recognized Student Organization, the Wichita State University Student Speech-Language-Hearing Association (WSUSSLHA). She has not just helped them build their schedules, register for classes, and find classrooms. She has helped them connect to the university, our Department, other students, and—most importantly—our professions so that they see themselves in the future as audiologists and speech-language pathologists. Carrie is receiving university recognition for 25 years of service. However, this recognition truly reflects service, not simply longevity at WSU. Her service record to WSU is notable. She has been a member of the Unclassified Professionals Senate, serving in several leadership roles (Senator/Secretary/Scholarship and Communications Chair) when the group was the University Staff Support Senate (2014 to 2016). As a member of the Council of University Women (since 2000), she served as the President/Scholarship Chair in the 2007 academic year. She is the Co-Chair of the CSD Faculty/Staff/Student Affairs Committee (since 2009). Regarding awards, she has been recognized multiple times for her service, including the CHP Optimization Award (2019), the President’s Distinguished Service award (2012), a Leadership Academy Senior Fellowship (2011), and the CHP Classified Staff Award (2011). Finally, she also serves the community beyond WSU as a member of the Young Professionals of Wichita (since 2008). Again, the Bender of Twigs Honor is not a “longevity award.” It is a recognition of service to WSU, one’s College, and one’s Department. As a Bender of Twigs Honoree, Carrie Wyatt is being recognized as a 25-year great ambassador of WSU, LAS/CHP, and CSD. It is an honor to be her Departmental colleague. Through her university service, she truly has earned the right to be a Bender of Twigs Honoree. Douglas Parham Chair and Program Director Communication Sciences and Disorders

title: Gamal Weheba
text: Gamal Weheba - Gamal Weheba Professor and ASQ Fellow Industrial, Systems, and Manufacturing Engineering Dr. Weheba joined our university in 2000, bringing with him a wealth of knowledge, a global perspective, and a deep commitment to excellence. Originally from Egypt, he earned his Ph.D. in Industrial Engineering from the University of Central Florida, and has since become a cornerstone of our College of Engineering. He has been a driving force in engineering education, research, student mentoring, and faculty advocacy at Wichita State University. Over the years, Dr. Weheba has distinguished himself as a Fellow of the American Society for Quality, contributing to foundational texts like the Certified Quality Engineer Handbook and co-authoring the widely used Manufacturing Processes & Materials textbook. His research in quality systems, additive manufacturing, and statistical process control has not only advanced academic knowledge but also shaped industry practices. Dr. Weheba has also played a vital role in organizing the Industry, Engineering & Management Systems Conference (IEMS), serving as Conference Chair and fostering collaboration across disciplines and borders. His editorial contributions to the Journal of Management and Engineering Integration (JMEI) have provided a platform for emerging voices and innovative research. His work has helped elevate the journal’s reputation and provided a platform for student-led research. Beyond his scholarship, Dr. Weheba has been a tireless advocate for faculty and students. As President of the AAUP-AFT chapter, he has stood up for academic freedom and student rights. His greatest legacy lies in the lives he has touched. Students recall how he stayed after class to help with projects, how he turned nervous students into confident researchers, and how his office, filled with books, prototypes, and ideas, became a hub of inspiration. Dr. Weheba’s industry collaborations include work with Spirit AeroSystems, international universities, and construction firms, bridging academic research with real-world impact. Dr. Weheba, on behalf of Wichita State University, your colleagues, your students, and the entire academic community, we thank you. Congratulations on 25 years of excellence! Deepak Gupta Department Chair and Graduate Program Coordinator

title: Jeff Pulaski
text: Jeff Pulaski - Jeff Pulaski Director, School of Art, Design and Creative Industries and Professor of Graphic Design Wichita State University It is my honor to reflect on 25 years of dedicated service of my colleague Jeff Pulaski and his induction into the Bender of Twigs. Jeff’s unwavering commitment to excellence, his passion for teaching, and his tireless advocacy for students have left an indelible mark on our campus community. Over the course of his career, Jeff has taught and mentored hundreds of students, collaborated with faculty across disciplines, and served on numerous committees throughout the School, College, and University. His leadership has been instrumental in shaping the future of arts education at WSU. In 2016, Jeff became Director of the School of Art, Design and Creative Industries, where he is now serving his third term. Under his leadership, the School has undergone significant growth and transformation. He successfully led the School through accreditation with the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD) and the internal WSU Program Review process—demonstrating his deep understanding of academic standards and institutional excellence. Jeff has also been a tireless advocate for improving campus facilities. He has worked closely with faculty, staff, and construction teams to address critical health and safety concerns in Henrion Hall and McKnight Art Center, ensuring that students have access to the resources and spaces they need to succeed. In addition to his administrative and teaching roles, Jeff is an active letterpress printer, researcher, and collector. His creative work has been exhibited at universities and museums across the United States, Ireland, England, and Australia. He has also shared his expertise internationally, leading letterpress workshops in Ireland, Greece, Cyprus, and Russia, further extending WSU’s global reach and reputation. His contributions have been recognized with the College of Fine Arts Excellence in Teaching Award (2012) and the Excellence in Special Fine Arts Endeavor Award (2018) for his significant contribution to the creation of the Bachelor of Applied Arts degree in Media Arts. That program has been so successful, it has become the School of Digital Arts with an enrollment of 500 students. Today, we proudly honor Jeff with induction into the honorary order of the Bender of Twigs, a fitting tribute to a career rooted in growth, resilience, and the nurturing of future generations. This recognition is a testament to the profound impact he has made—and continues to make—on our institution and all who have had the privilege of working alongside him. Congratulations, Jeff, and thank you for 25 years of extraordinary service. Wendy Hanes Assistant Dean, College of Fine Arts

title: Jodi Pelkowski
text: Jodi Pelkowski - Jodi Pelkowski Bill and Shelly Moore Faculty Fellow and Associate Professor Economics Barton School of Business It is an honor to reflect on the 25 years of service that my friend and colleague, Jodi Pelkowski, Bill and Shelley Moore Faculty Fellow, has given to Wichita State University. Her tenure at WSU came about because Jodi’s mentor at Kentucky was a friend of mine from grad school. Mark told her I was happy at WSU, and that she should check out the position here. Former Associate Professor and Dean Jim Clark and I were tasked with meeting Jodi and showing her around during her campus visit. Within five minutes, we were convinced that we needed to do whatever it took to get her to come to Wichita State. It helped that it was a beautiful, warm, sunny day when Jodi visited, and when she asked if it was always like this in Wichita in the winter, we lied and said yes. Jodi quickly made her mark at WSU, achieving tenure and promotion within the requisite six years and winning a slew of awards ever since: 2006: WSU Excellence in Teaching Award 2006: Outstanding Nominee for the Academy for Effective Teaching and Research Excellence 2007 AND 2016: Graduate Instructor of the Year 2018: WSU Academy for Effective Teaching Award 2019: TAN Excellence in Undergraduate Advising Award 2022: Barton School of Business Undergraduate Instructor of the Year What makes all this more amazing is that during this time she served as undergraduate coordinator for the economics major. This is an unpaid position which takes a lot of time and effort but does not count for much toward tenure and promotion. Economics did not have a student group, so she created Economists Anonymous to fill that void. Economists Anonymous is now an active student group with lots of members, events and projects. During her time as undergraduate coordinator, the number of students with economics as their major or minor greatly increased. She still spends a lot of time writing letters of recommendation, and her connections with Wichita area businesses help students get great internships while in school and good paying jobs after they graduate. Currently, Jodi is involved with a small team of students who meet on Saturdays to work on a project for Textron, which will certainly enhance their job prospects when they graduate. Jodi is passionate about helping students. The Barton School of Business does not have a lot of honors courses, so Jodi regularly does extra work, again unpaid, to give students the option to have Econ 202 as an honors course. Last February, Jodi was asked to revive Beta Gamma Sigma, the business honorary society, which had basically been abandoned or years. Before the end of the school year, we were celebrating inductees at a banquet. Jodi and her husband Pat have a licensed and insured liquor catering service called Shaken or Stirred. They are active in community events like Wine and Dine-Osaurs at Field Station: Dinosaurs in Derby and many WSU sporting events. Jodi therefore has instant credibility and can give many real-world, local examples of applying economic concepts to business. Jodi is also a wonderful colleague. She has taught classes for me when I am attending conferences, given advice for handling problem students and generally been there for me, for other colleagues, and most importantly for students. She is indeed already a Bender of the Twig! Jan Wolcutt Senior Educator, Department of Economics

title: John Hetzendorf
text: John Hetzendorf - John Hetzendorf Shocker Throws Coach Wichita State University Track and Field John Hetzendorf, known simply as “Dorf” to all who know and love him has been the heart of Shocker Throws for 25 years, transforming athletes not just into better throwers but into awesome people. Before coming to Shocker Nation, Hetzendorf graduated from Kent State University, where he was a two-time Division I All-American in the javelin. He competed professionally as a world-class athlete for several years and threw in multiple USA Track and Field Championship meets, Olympic Trials, and the 2005 World Championships. It was always a treat to watch Dorf compete! From recruitment to one-on-one meetings to set goals and formulate personalized training plans, Dorf goes above and beyond for everyone around him. I met Dorf in 2001 when he recruited me to WSU. Unlike other coaches who just called, Dorf came to one of my high school basketball games and congratulated me afterward. His genuine care and dedication helped lead me and many others to make one of the most transformative decisions of our lives: becoming a Shocker. His dedication is unmatched, not just to the sport, but to the people in it. His compassion is woven into all he does. Watching him throw, coach, and connect with others shows how much he genuinely cares. Dorf’s coaching style isn’t just about technique or distance; it’s about heart, grit, and learning to “trust the process” through our failures. He pours as much energy into others as they are willing to give and pushes each person to become their best self. One of Dorf’s greatest gifts is his ability to see potential in others. He believed in me and numerous others long before we believed in ourselves. His mentorship helped us chase goals and experience things we couldn’t have imagined possible. He’s not just a coach or coworker; he humbly uplifts, encourages, and empowers others. Years beyond anyone’s time on the runway or in the ring, Dorf checks in just to say hi, offers support during life’s challenges, and shares Shocker Track updates with his signature Dorf style. Dorf is a guy who will do anything for anyone, whether he helps a friend move, spends countless hours coaching, offers a kind, listening ear, or makes the throws squad laugh hysterically as he rips up a heart-shaped Rice Crispy treat to lighten the mood when a team member is having bad luck with love. He’s always ready to share his legendary humor and positivity to make any bad day better. Beyond his selflessness, Dorf is very intelligent and humbly puts his biology degree to excellent use as a coach, seamlessly connecting concepts in weightlifting, nutrition, and injury prevention. If you didn’t know he studied biology, you may think he studied engineering or art. His freehand drawing of WuShock is one of the best I’ve ever seen, and he’s always ready to innovate and solve complex problems like inventing creative training tools so his athletes improve by gaining specific strength. We are truly blessed to have Dorf as the face of Shocker Throws for all these years, coaching numerous student-athletes to conference titles, school records, All-America awards, NCAA Championships, Olympic Trials, and more. Here’s to many more years of you side sipping a Dr. Pepper while you build up and encourage young throwers as they develop into wonderful, passion-filled men and women. Like so many others, my life would be very different without Dorf’s influence. Thank you, Dorf, for being the best big brother, noble mentor, and a genuine friend! Chandra Cralle Proud WSU Track and Field Alum 2005 - 2007 WSU Admissions Regional Recruitment Manager- TX

title: Mark Schneegurt
text: Mark Schneegurt - Mark Schneegurt Professor, Biological Sciences Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences Dr. Mark A. Schneegurt is an author, educator, scientist, and entrepreneur. He holds degrees from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Brown University, with professional appointments at Eli Lilly, Purdue University, and University of Notre Dame. In 2000, he joined the Department of Biological Sciences at Wichita State University, rising to the rank of Full Professor. As a founder of the Department of Biomedical Engineering, Dr. Schneegurt remains an affiliated faculty member. He was previously affiliated faculty in the Department of Curriculum and Instruction. Currently, he is an affiliated faculty member in the Department of History. For several years, he was Faculty of Excellence as a Coleman Foundation Faculty Fellow in Entrepreneurship. Dr. Schneegurt teaches General Biology I for 100+ students at a time and teaches a large General Microbiology course. He prefers large classes, especially at lower levels, given their showmanship and the fresh realizations of naïve students. Over the years, he has developed and offered new upper division courses including Applied and Environmental Microbiology and Astrobiology. His pioneering course Interstellar Seminar has been celebrated worldwide. While not an awardee, Dr. Schneegurt was a Finalist for the Academy of Effective Teaching Award on two occasions. He has received the Leadership in the Advancement in Teaching Award, offering the first full online course in LAS. Dr. Schneegurt has been instrumental in developing the Masters of Earth, Environmental, and Physical Sciences, Associate of Science degrees in the sciences, the current Forensic Science degree, the new Forensic Biology MS degree, and the Certificate in Genetic Counseling. Outreach education has been an important part of Dr. Schneegurt's career. Starting with a small award from KanEd for developing classroom activities using household materials, through an award from Kansas NSF EPSCoR, and ultimately with a $1M NSF GK-12 award, the Pass Me the Salt project maintained programs in all comprehensive high schools in the Wichita Public Schools, sending WSU science students into classrooms, creating in-school research clubs, and publishing papers in peer-reviewed scientific journals with high school students and their teachers as authors. He helped lead the science cafe program of public talks in Wichita using his connection to Sigma Xi, the Scientific Research Honor Society, for which he has been President of the WSU Chapter for decades. Dr. Schneegurt was lead writer for OpenStax Microbiology , an OER textbook that is free for students and is currently the most widely used college microbiology textbook, saving students millions of dollars. Dr. Schneegurt's love of scientific research began as a child, particularly his interest in space sciences. He has held extramural research grants for 30 years, the entire time he has been at WSU. His laboratory has supported 15 or more research students continuously, both graduates and undergraduates, and has hosted pre-college students and teachers. Dr. Schneegurt was a recipient of the WSU Excellence in Research Award, the KINBRE Faculty Scholar Award, and named one of the 150 Greatest Scientists in the History of Kansas by Ad Astra. He arrived at WSU with three active grants in environmental science, one of which resulted in a paper in Science . His most important work at WSU began with projects at the Great Salt Plains of Oklahoma, an extremely salty environment. An early NSF Microbial Observatories award of $1M established Dr. Schneegurt as a leader in the microbiology of extremophiles. Salty environments are found throughout the solar system, so his work attracted the attention of NASA, starting decades-long collaborations with Jet Propulsion Laboratory and a series of astrobiology grants from NASA Planetary Protection. Dr. Schneegurt has wide research interests beyond astrobiology, including publications in environmental metal pollution, agricultural soil nitrogen cycles, avian microbiology, wastewater treatment, medical therapeutics, and algal biodiesel, among others. He obtained funding for the first permanent building at the Biological Field Station. His research has generated millions of dollars in extramural funding. Dr. Schneegurt has delivered more than 250 public presentations and published more than 100 papers in scientific journals and books, nearly all with WSU student authors. Outside of science, Dr. Schneegurt has pursued a second academic interest in philology and history. This includes popular works, such as a series of travel books on The Beatles. His more scholarly works have been with religious texts. He has published the first translations of the poetry of Ephraim Kuh, a Haskalah epigrammatist in the 18th century. His most well-known work has been exploring the Inquisition trial transcripts of crypto-Jews in colonial Mexico. A published collection of religious poems and prayers from these transcripts is the most comprehensive to date and has led to presentations, grant proposals, invited articles, and even a recital of the songs set to music again after 400 years. Initially a passion project, this work has attracted collaborators worldwide and is contributing to outreach to the descendants of conversos today. Mark Schneegurt Professor, Biological Sciences

title: Mehmet Barut
text: Mehmet Barut - Mehmet Barut Chair, Associate Professor, and Director of Supply Chain Graduate Programs Finance Real Estate and Decision Science Barton School of Business It is a pleasure to celebrate my colleague and friend, Dr. Mehmet Barut, as he is recognized for twenty-five years of dedicated service to Wichita State University. Throughout his career, Mehmet has exemplified strategic leadership, kindness, and a steadfast commitment to elevating both people and programs across the Barton School of Business and the University. Mehmet’s WSU journey began in 2000, and over the next quarter century he rose through the academic ranks to Professor, taking on roles that shaped programs, people, and strategy across the university. Today, he serves as Chair of the Department of Finance, Real Estate, and Decision Sciences (FREDS) and as Director for Graduate Programs in Supply Chain Management—positions that reflect the trust our campus places in his vision and stewardship. Mehmet’s university service is both vast and consequential. He led the Faculty Senate as President in 2014–2015, guided numerous committees and task forces, and continues to advise through the Past Presidents Council—steady leadership that has advanced governance and faculty success. Within the Barton School, he has poured his energy into strategic planning, graduate curriculum development, faculty recruitment, and student support—quietly doing the work that builds strong academic programs. Perhaps his most visible legacy is the founding of the Master’s of Science in Supply Chain Management, a program he proposed and launched in 2018. As its director, he has significantly grown enrollment, built strong bridges between academia and industry, and aligned the curriculum with the needs of employers—advancing Wichita State’s applied learning mission. Mehmet also helped design and lead the Cargill Graduate Certificate in Supply Chain Management, expanding WSU’s reach to working professionals and deepening the university’s partnership with one of the region’s most impactful employers. That initiative opened doors for learners while showcasing the Barton School’s ability to co-create talent pipelines with industry. His external engagement extends beyond Cargill to collaborations with ISM-Wichita, WSU Tech, and other community and professional organizations that expand opportunities for students and strengthen industry connections. As a scholar, Mehmet has published 20 peer-reviewed journal articles, delivered more than 40 conference presentations, and secured over $150,000 in internal and external grants to support his research and teaching. His studies in operations and supply chain management have advanced both theory and practice, earning him recognition as the Barton School Researcher of the Year in 2020. As department chair, Mehmet’s leadership is marked by integrity, inclusion, and an ability to elevate every conversation. Colleagues know him as a thoughtful listener who introduces new ideas and better ways to achieve shared goals. His talent for uniting people around purpose has strengthened programs, partnerships, and morale across the Barton School and the university community. Across teaching, research, and service, Mehmet’s through-line is simple and profound: he builds programs that help people thrive. He models the best of what it means to be a Shocker—curious, collaborative, and deeply committed to excellence and the common good. Chris Broberg Associate Dean, Faculty & Research Interim Director, Center for Entrepreneurship Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship

title: Travis Feeney
text: Travis Feeney - Travis Feeney Executive Director, TRIO Educational Opportunity Centers College Readiness/Retention Programs When I first learned that I had been chosen to share comments in honor of Travis Feeney, I felt deeply honored and genuinely excited. It is a gratifying moment to celebrate someone who so perfectly embodies what it means to be a “Bender of Twigs.” Just as faculty and staff help guide students in their pursuit of knowledge, Travis exemplifies that spirit. I first met Travis in 1999, and little did I know the remarkable journey that lay ahead with him as both a colleague and a friend. The personal memories of his personal and professional growth are deeply etched in my mind—from celebrating his and Christina’s wedding, to walking with him through the passing of his father, to hearing the joyful stories of his mother’s missionary travels and watching his unwavering devotion to his family. Even to this day, when his mother, Ms. Sue Feeney, calls him or needs something, Travis answers, and he does it. That simple truth says everything about his character: loyal, compassionate, and grounded in love and service. Walking with Travis on his professional journey has been the best live movie ever, filled with growth, inspiration, laughter, and moments that could only be scripted by life itself. Over the years, Travis has transformed from a quiet, hardworking professional into a beacon for education and a shining example that education truly is the passport to success. His career began as a student assistant with TRIO Upward Bound Wichita Prep (UBWP) in 1992. Since then, he has remained steadfast in his mission to champion first-generation and low-income students. Travis earned his Bachelor’s in Business Administration and, most recently, his Master’s in Public Administration, both from Wichita State University. In June 2024, after completing his master’s degree, he transitioned from UBWP to become the Executive Director for TRIO Educational Opportunity Centers (EOC), where he now empowers adult learners to pursue their educational dreams. Under his leadership, EOC has become a trusted name in the community—connecting people and organizations with Wichita State University in ways that truly embody Shocker Pride. Travis is no longer the quiet one. Though he still moves with calm precision, his actions, energy, and vision speak volumes. He is strategic, analytical, and deeply impactful. Congratulations, Travis, on 25 years of extraordinary service, unwavering dedication, and the countless lives you have helped shape. Rhonda Hicks Program Director , College Readiness/Retention Programs

title: Bender of Twigs
text: Bender of Twigs - History & Past Honorees Bender of Twigs was conceived in 1951 by then University of Wichita President Harry Corbin (1949-1963), his assistant Kathryn Griffith and English professor Bill Nelson. This unique designation is bestowed upon employees who have served 25 years of service to Wichita State University. The name "Bender of Twigs" is a reference to the similarity between the way a young sapling bends toward the light as it grows and how faculty and staff help lead the student in their search for knowledge. In Bender of Twigs tradition, each honoree chooses a friend or colleague to provide written remarks on their behalf and these are presented to the honorees, along with a framed certificate of their induction into the Order. The Citation of the Certificate was written by Bill Nelson, professor emeritus of English and reads: “To all persons to whom these presents may come greeting, be it known to all wielders of the rod, leaners on the lectern, pupilmongers and pedagogues, as well as pencil pushers, mainframe methodologists, memo maniacs, procedure pathologies, office ontologists , and computer compulsives, and also the tidiers , tillers, toilers and Cushman cowboys that, having completed twenty-five years of faithful service for the honorary order of Bender of Twigs, has accordingly been admitted to that order with all rights, privileges and immunities thereunto pertaining in witness whereof we have caused this diploma to be signed by the President of the University and our corporate seal to be hereto affixed in the City of Wichita.. .” 2020-2024 2024 Name Dept. title: LevelUp Your Leadership Program
text: LevelUp Your Leadership Program - The LevelUp Your Leadership Program is a “choose your own adventure” style program, allowing you to pick and choose courses from the program’s catalog based on your unique leadership development needs. There are introductory level courses for those career pathing to a leader role or those brand new to a leader role. There is a core set of courses accompanied by a certificate of completion for existing leaders looking to level up their leadership knowledge and skills. Watch this short video to learn about the program and start your journey today! NOTE: Go to myTraining to complete this video if you’d like credit for it on your transcript. Course Catalog Go to myTraining and find the LevelUp Your Leadership Program Curriculum to see all available courses and start your journey today! CERTIFICATE PATH Role of a Leader Instructor-led 1 hour 30 minutes Recommended for all levels Forget the org chart. Real management happens in the moments between meetings, in the decisions made under pressure, and in the relationships that hold teams together. In this session, we explore Henry Mintzberg's landmark framework for understanding what managers actually do and why it still matters decades after it was first introduced. Through his three core role categories (Interpersonal, Informational, and Decisional) Mintzberg cuts through management theory to reveal the ten distinct roles every effective supervisor plays. Whether you're new to supervision or a seasoned leader looking to sharpen your self-awareness, this session offers a practical lens for reflecting on your own management style, identifying your strengths, and recognizing where you may have blind spots. You'll leave with a clearer picture of the full scope of the managerial role and a new vocabulary for talking about the work you do every day. Building Relationships and Getting Results (coming fall 2026) Instructor-led Available to all levels Learn how to build and nurture relationships with your team and across the organization, how to create a shared understanding of expectations and goals, and how they bolster one another Change Management (coming fall 2026) Instructor-led Available to those in a leadership role Learn your role and responsibilities in managing change and how to manage it successfully whether it’s a change you initiated or a change pushed out by the larger department or organization Improving Culture Through Difficult Conversations Instructor-led 1 hour Recommended for all levels Difficult conversations are essential to fostering a healthy team culture. In this session, you’ll learn how our Shocker PROUD Service Standards help establish behavioral norms, a framework for navigating difficult conversations effectively, and strategies to hold each other accountable while maintaining professionalism, responsiveness, openness, understanding, and dependability. Coaching and Corrective Action Case Study (coming summer 2026) Instructor-led Available to those currently in a leader role Learn about the coaching and corrective action process and practice effectively applying it. Maximizing Staff Performance Reviews (coming fall 2026) Instructor-led Recommended for anyone with non-teaching, benefit-eligible direct reports Learn about the performance evaluation process and how to leverage it as a tool in driving employee engagement. Student Success Focus (coming fall 2026) Instructor-led Available for all levels Learn effective strategies and share best practices for fostering student success and persistence. Using Reason to Resolve Conflict Instructor-led 1 hour Recommended for all levels Whether they take place in the workplace or in one’s personal life, conflicts are inevitable; however, that does not mean that they must always be damaging. When emotions are understood and reason is used to handle conflict, the result can actually be strengthened relationships rather than damaged ones. This workshop discusses how you can replace pure emotion with rational decision-making when dealing with conflict. RECOMMENDED COURSES Transitioning from Peer to Leader (coming fall 2026) Online module Recommended for those career pathing to a leader role and those new to a leader role Learn the key shifts between individual contributor to people leader and tactics for a successful transition Increased Effectiveness (coming fall 2026) Online module Available for all levels Learn tips and tricks to better manage your time. Motivating Your Team Online module 1 hour Recommended for those currently in a leader role Knowing how to motivate a team is more important than ever, given the pace of change, competitive demands, and increasing diversity of most organizations. This course shows you how to bring out the best in every member of your team, using proven motivation and employee engagement techniques. Learn how to create a strong foundation built on a shared vision and values and empower each team member to deliver excellent service. See how coaching can help you develop stronger relationships and how to leverage incentives that really work. Since positive results depend so much on effective leadership, this course also identifies the skills you need to build an organization that thrives. Each section is filled with real-world examples and tips to get your team from good to great. Emotional Intelligence Instructor-led 1 hour Available to all levels Implementing discipline over our emotional life is difficult and requires lifelong practice. Being able to choose to act or respond in a particular manner is preferable to re-acting on a consistent basis, yet it is difficult. Enhancing emotional intelligence improves our ability to master our emotional functioning. High emotional intelligence can improve our communications with all others, enhance our perception of satisfaction with ourselves and our lives and increase our productiveness overall. Building Team Culture (coming fall 2026) Instructor-led Available to those in a leadership role Learn the importance of team culture, your role in building a strong team and university culture, and tactics for creating and sustaining it. Effective Hiring Practices (coming fall 2026) Instructor-led Recommended for anyone that participates in interviewing candidates Learn tactics for an effective hiring process including the do’s and don’ts of interviews and the role of a search committee. Helpful Tools and Resources (coming summer 2026) Online module Available for all levels Learn about a variety of tools and resources vital to carrying out your responsibilities as a leader. LevelUp Your Leadership Certificate Path Recognition Below is a list of your colleagues who have completed the LevelUp Your Leadership certificate path. List of people who completed the LevelUp Your Leadership certificate path. First Name Last Name Department #Your #Name #Here Will you be the first to complete the certificate path? Contact Information Would you like to contact somebody in the Human Resources Organizational Development department? Our team has a dedicated group inbox that is checked frequently by all of our team members on a regular basis. Select the link below to get started? HR.OrganizationalDevelopment@wichita.edu

title: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist
text: Non-Benefit Eligible International Student Employment Checklist - 1) Arrive in the United States Welcome! We’re happy you’re here. 2) Enroll in Classes You can enroll in classes after you complete the following steps: Arrive in Wichita. Complete the check-in process with the International Education department. Meet with your academic advisor. 3) Search and Apply for On-Campus Employment Most on-campus positions are posted on Shocker Central . Use your myWSU ID and password to log in. If you have questions or need more information about Shocker Central call the Shocker Career Accelerator at (316) 978-3688, or email us at SCA@wichita.edu . 4) Get a Job Offer You will need to receive an official offer. The Hiring Manager must complete the International Job Offer Form in BLUE ink. At this time, your Hiring Manager will also submit a Non-Benefit Eligible Hiring Form, which indicates to Human Resources they wish to hire you for an on-campus position. 5) Request Employment Eligibility Verification Take your completed International Job Offer Form and I-94 to the International Education Department located in the Garvey International Center (GI) at 3203 E. 17 th Street N. Wichita, KS 67208. If you need help finding this building, use this interactive map. Your I-94 can be obtained on the Customs and Border Protection site. 6) Pick up your Employment Eligibility Verification (EEV) at International Education After documents are provided, International Education will prepare your Employment Eligibility Verification (EEV) within 2-4 business days. You will be contacted when your EVV is ready to be picked up at the Garvey International Center. 7) Complete the online application for a Social Security Number After you receive your Employment Eligibility Verification (EVV), complete the online application for a Social Security Number. 8) Complete In-Person Meeting at the Social Security Administration office Go to the Social Security Administration office to show the appropriate documentation. The International Job Offer completed by a campus department. Employment Eligibility Verification prepared by International Education. Continued Attendance I-20 (for F-1 students) or DS-2019 with work authorization (for J-1 students). Valid passport and I-94. The local Social Security Administration office is located at 3216 N Cypress Street, Wichita, Kansas 67226. Visit Social Security Administration for office hours and additional information. 9) Wait for Social Security Card to Arrive The card will arrive via mail and on average can take two weeks. 10) Receive Social Security Card The card will arrive via mail and on average can take two weeks. 11) Complete all Onboarding Tasks You cannot complete necessary forms until your Social Security card has been received. At that time, complete all onboarding tasks assigned by Human Resources. These tasks will be received via email. Human Resources cannot put you into WSU’s system without all forms completed. 12) Complete I-9 Human Resources allows walk-in appointments to complete your I-9 Form; however, you can also schedule a specific appointment. Please use our online scheduling tool to set up an appointment to complete Section 2 of the Form I-9. Bring all necessary documentation which proves eligibility to work at Wichita State University as an International Student. 13) Your Hiring Manager will submit an electronic personnel action form (ePAF) Your Hiring Manager will submit an electronic personnel form (ePAF). title: Background Check and Guide
text: Background Check and Guide - Background Check and Guide Background checks are completed for employees (including student employees) and volunteers, per Policy 3.31 Background Checks for Employment . The University uses a third party vendor to perform criminal history and sex offender background checks. Information regarding the requirement for background checks is found below. Driver’s license checks are processed dependent upon position requirements. Departments are only notified by Human Resources regarding the results of a background check for employees if the results are flagged. The completion date of background checks are entered into Banner by Human Resources, and can be found in WSU Reporting. Each department pays for background checks for their respective positions. Background Check Requirements Benefit Eligible Employees (New or Rehire) Required if no background check is on file OR if break in service is one year or more, upon returning to the University Current employees moving to new positions at WSU Required if no background check is on file Graduate Student Employees Domestic – Required with first graduate assistantship. Also required when rehired and no background check is on file, or if break in service is one year or more upon returning to the University. International – Not required. Background checks conducted by Federal Homeland Security as part of the visa process are considered acceptable for employment purposes. Lecturers Required if no background check is on file OR If break in service is one year or more, upon returning to the University Regular/Work Study Student Employees Domestic – Required IF the position requires handling of financial transactions or requires direct interaction with minors, or the student will perform work on a project where a background check is required by contract or a third party. International – Not required. Background checks conducted by Federal Homeland Security as part of the visa process are considered acceptable for employment purposes. Temporary Employees (U3/U4) Required if position will last 6 months or longer, OR if the position requires handling of financial transactions or requires direct interaction with minors. Required when rehired and no background check is on file or if break in service is one year or more upon returning to the University. Volunteers Required if the position requires handling of financial transactions or requires direct interaction with minors. Department contact will be notified of background check results. title: Import/Export Considerations
text: Import/Export Considerations - Import/Export Considerations when Hiring When applicable, work and research undertaken at WSU requires proper handling, using, and safeguarding of information that is subject to U.S. Export Control Regulations by federal law. Access to federally export-controlled Information is a privilege. Unauthorized access, use for an unpermitted purpose, and or mismanagement of such information risk economic and strategic injury to the information owner and reputational harm and legal complications for Wichita State University and yourself. Researchers may be held personally liable for violations of such terms and regulations. No one wants to be on the wrong side of the law, and this is where the Office of Export Controls & Compliance (“ECO”) comes in. The office is dedicated to helping all areas at WSU flourish in its compliance with these regulations, and can be contacted at exportcontrols@wichita.edu or (316) 978-COMP. For a general primer on what “Export Controls” refers to, what your responsibilities are, and what triggers export control law and research security concerns at Wichita State, see the “General Guidelines” below. What does this have to do with hiring employees? The bottom line is that when there are export compliance or regulatory research security matters at hand, they drastically affect how you may go about filling a position. In some cases, due to the type of work being done, US personhood, establishing a TCP, or gathering a license by a federal agency may be required. Issues related to dual citizenship, country of birth or interactions with a sanctioned country or university may also come into play during the hiring process, as well as OFAC-related concerns such as denied entities and restricted parties. While maintaining compliance export laws, we also must ensure continued compliance with federal labor laws, making sure that these restrictions are only used when necessitated by federal regulation. For this reason, it is important to understand the impact of export compliance before posting a position so that any restrictions on applicants can be included with the ad. Again, for a general primer on what “Export Controls” refers to, what your responsibilities are, and what triggers export control law and research security concerns at Wichita State, see the “General Guidelines” below. In order to determine if Export Control review and approval is necessary for your new hire, please see and utilize the Export Control Hiring Checklist . If export control review and approval is required for submitting your job posting, then we cannot proceed with the process until approval has been received by the Export Compliance Officer. General Guidelines As a general note, a foreign national hire (i.e., a hire who is not either a U.S. Citizen or a U.S. Permanent Resident/“Green Card”-holder) can only have access to data, information, projects, and research that meets the definition of Fundamental Research (definition below), absent approval by the Export Control Office. It is the job of the applicant’s supervisor to ensure that such an applicant only has access to fundamental research until such access has been approved by the ECO. The definition of “Fundamental Research” as provided in 15 CFR § 734.8, is: "...basic and applied [information or] research... where the resulting information is ordinarily published and shared broadly in the research community, as distinguished from proprietary research and from industrial development, design, production, and product utilization, the results of which ordinarily are restricted for proprietary or national security reasons." Wichita State University is a federal contractor. Compliance with such federal and state laws is critical to being able to conduct business here at Wichita State. Wichita State University is required to certify or assure state and federal governments that the University complies with relevant statutes, administrative orders, etc. As the applicant’s supervisor, it is your responsibility to ensure compliance with access restrictions that may be placed on certain hires. It is your responsibility to reach out to the Office of Export Controls & Compliance if there are any questions or concerns on these terms and/or export controls and how it pertains to the applicant’s involvement in research or their work at WSU. It is your responsibility to seek approval through the Office of Export Controls & Compliance prior to allowing the applicant any access to proprietary, controlled, or confidential data, information, or technology, or any export-controlled information or data or information covered on a Technology Control Plan. Pursuant to the Arms Export Control Act (Title 22, U.S.C., Sec 2751, et seq.) and the Export Administration Act of 1979 (Title 50, U.S.C., App. 2401 et seq.), violations are subject to severe criminal penalties. Training on relevant laws & regulations pertaining to research security and export controls is available for your group and/or new hires. Please reach out the Export Control Office with any request for training(s). If you plan on working with NIAR/IDP at WSU in any capacity, please ensure to reach out to exportcontrols@wichita.edu prior to engaging, as much of the programs done under the IDP umbrella is subject to various research security & export controls. The below notes are general guidelines when beginning to assess if there are export control needs for your role, lab, and/or office. They have been adapted from this column on How Export Controls Impact Nearly All Corners of the University. Research Research or information that does not fall under the definition of fundamental research is export controlled, such as: Research in science and engineering, particularly when sponsor- or externally-funded, which includes a proprietary component and is not intended for open publishing or educational purposes. Military, energy, biological, or space research which limits access or dissemination. Non-engineering research, such as in sociology, medicine, or marketing, which includes a proprietary component. Any proprietary research or information, such as information disclosed under an NDA, restricted to the public. Research funded by the U.S. Government, especially within the Department of Defense. Cutting-edge research in computer science or information technology. If you plan on taking on externally-funded work which involves a proprietary component or restricts access or dissemination, first reach out to exportcontrols@wichita.edu to ensure compliance prior to engaging with any foreign nationals, including students. International Travel & Collaboration with non-U.S. Persons Any international travel, including controlled information "traveling" with you or being "sent" over international borders, whether in physical or conceptual form, are subject to export controls. Certain destinations, e.g., embargoed and sanctioned countries, may not be traversable. What you are allowed to travel with (physical items) or discuss (information) with foreign persons or within foreign destinations will always depend on the specific details of your situation, including the content of your collaboration and the destination country at hand. Export controlled technical data is considered a “deemed export” if it is accessed by or shared with a foreign national, even within U.S. borders on a university campus. If you are travelling internationally or collaborating with foreign persons or entities for research or work, first reach out to exportcontrols@wichita.edu to ensure compliance. International Shipping All international shipments, except a few items such as previously published material, are subject to export controls. If you are shipping an item internationally, first reach out to exportcontrols@wichita.edu to ensure compliance. International collaboration with Foreign Entities or Persons, or Denied Entities or Persons Foreign citizens of certain countries, even if holding a valid work visa, may not be eligible to be involved in certain export-controlled work or information. Certain activities and collaborations with OFAC-denied entities or persons will not be feasible. If you plan on taking on any international collaborations, or accepting any funds for research from a non-U.S. entity, be sure to first reach out to exportcontrols@wichita.edu to ensure compliance. What Research, Types of Items, Information, or Technology is NOT Subject to Export Controls? Information already published, or publicly-accessible information (such as that which can be found online, published technical data, information made available through unlimited distribution at a conference or exhibition). Information classifying as fundamental research, with no publication restrictions or restrictions on access to results. General mathematical, scientific, or engineering principles, as well as information taught within an educational context such as through university courses. Usually, foreign-origin items temporarily in the U.S. are not subject to Export Controls. When Should You Contact the Export Compliance Office for Help? Here are a few red flags that might indicate you need to give us a call: You're not sure if the item you're exporting is allowed or restricted under current laws and regulations. You're working on a research project and you think it might have proprietary, military, or national security implications. You're planning on attending a conference or workshop in another country and you're not sure if you need to get any special approvals. You're planning on inviting a foreign researcher for collaboration, whether they are domestic or abroad. You're planning on traveling abroad with research equipment, sending a package to a colleague in another country, or even sharing certain types of information with someone from another country, and you're not sure if you're in compliance. Navigating the waters of Export Compliance can indeed be some very tricky business, and this is only compounded within WSU's environment as an international state research and academic institution. Thankfully, the Office of Export Controls & Compliance is here to lend a helping hand in all matters export-compliance. The office has a direct email address for questions, exportcontrols@wichita.edu , or you may call 978-COMP. Please do not hesitate to send an email or call with any questions you might have - at any level of specificity or generality! SME: 2/06/18 MH Revised: 09/25/2024 NH

title: Interviewing Applicants
text: Interviewing Applicants - Interview Preparation/ Development This section provides information on many components involved with the interview process: developing appropriate interview questions, structuring the interview, and handling hospitality expenses. Developing Interview Questions Types of Interview Questions Structuring the Interview Conducting Multiple Interviews Developing Interview Questions The goal of the interview is to determine the knowledge, skills, and abilities of a prospective employee. It should be conducted so that it provides as much information as possible about an applicant's potential to perform the duties of a particular position. To do this, the interview questions and process must be developed with this goal in mind. When developing interview questions, the questions should be job specific and appropriate for the complexity and level of the position. They should also relate to the position requirements on the PeopleAdmin position description . During this development, you will need to determine what type of interview questions to include and how they will be evaluated. Compliance is also an important consideration during the interview process. Interviewers must be consistent throughout the interview process, making sure both the format of the interviews and the basic questions asked of each candidate are the same. Types of Interview Questions 1. The types of interview questions used are determined by the type of information you are attempting to gain from the candidate. General knowledge interview questions may be used to verify certain information or knowledge. Tell me about your CPA experience. Tell me about your experience working with students in a higher education setting. Can you elaborate on your education? Have you completed your degree program? What medical licenses or certifications do you currently hold? Questions aimed at clarifying information provided on application documentation would also fall into this category. Behavioral interview questions are used to determine how a candidate dealt with specific job related situations. The information provided by the candidate is then analyzed in an attempt to determine how they may respond to similar situations in the future. What do you do when your schedule is interrupted? Give an example of how you handle it. Tell me about the most difficult co-worker you have worked with. How was he or she difficult? Have you handled a difficult situation with a client or customer? How? Have you ever made a mistake? How did you handle it? Situational interview questions are similar to behavioral interview questions. Instead of asking about past situations, the candidate is presented with scenarios and asked how they would respond in the given situation. It's 2 p.m. and you have a critical report due to your manager at 4:00 p.m. A very important customer calls with a crisis, needing your immediate attention. How would you respond? 2. Human Resources has made available a comprehensive list of acceptable interview questions . 3. The law is very clear about the types of questions that may not be asked during the interview process. It is unlawful to discriminate against anyone in any aspect of employment or the employment process on the basis of age, race, sex, national origin, religion, creed, color, disability status or disabled veteran's status, sexual orientation, citizenship or impending citizenship. Any concerns about the appropriateness of questions relating to any of these areas should be discussed with the Office of Human Resources prior to conducting interviews. Irrelevant or “nice to know” questions should never be asked. The following information should be obtained, if needed, only after the person has accepted an offer of employment. Questions related to candidate name that might indicate marital status, ancestry, national origin or descent are inappropriate. Age related questions are only appropriate if there if age is a legal requirement (i.e. must be 18 years or older to work here). If age is not a legal requirement for the position, all questions that could be considered age related should be avoided (i.e. “When did you graduate from high school?”). NOTE: The Kansas Act Against Discrimination prohibits discrimination against persons age 18 and over. No questions should be asked related to race or color, gender, ancestry, national origin, or birthplace. Do not ask questions related to marital status or family status. This would include questions related to pregnancy, the number of children in the household, or child care availability. Do not ask candidates about their native language. Questions related to religion should be avoided. Candidates should be given the hours and days of their work schedule. Employers must make reasonable accommodations for an employee’s religious practices. Should you encounter a situation where a candidate requests accommodation, please contact the Office of Human Resources. No questions should be asked about a candidates arrest records. Questions concerning convictions may be asked if job related. Questions related to citizenship should be avoided unless the position has ITAR restrictions concerning citizenship. For candidates with military service, questions related to the type of discharge are not allowable. Credit report information or other types of financial data should not be a part of the interview process unless it is a business necessity to have this information. This includes garnishments and filing for bankruptcy. Please contact the Office of Human Resources for more information on this topic. Do not ask candidates about home ownership. Candidates with Disabilities - The Americans with Disabilities Act ("ADA") prohibits employers from asking disability-related questions to employment applicants. A "disability-related question" is any question that is likely to elicit information about disability. Under the ADA, an employer cannot lawfully ask an applicant whether he has a particular disability nor ask questions that are closely related to a disability. During the interview process, the candidate can be asked about their ability to perform the essential functions of the job for which he or she is applying, with or without reasonable accommodation. Other problematic types of questions: What does your wife do for a living? Have you experienced any significant illness in the past year? How long to you plan to work before retiring? Where did you grow up? THE BOTTOM LINE – IF IT IS NOT JOB SPECIFIC, DO NOT ASK THE QUESTION. 4. When developing your interview questions, make sure to include those aimed at clarifying information provided on application documentation. There are often items that are hard to score or cannot be scored. Make sure to address these. 5. It is best practice to notate which question relates to which criteria. For example: “As you know, this position will assist small business owners. Therefore we require three years of experience working with the public, please explain in detail your experience. (Required #3)” “As a curator for the Ulrich Museum there may be opportunities for educational presentations. Explain your teaching experience within the context of an art museum. (Preferred #2)” 6. Fit questions should be designed to determine if a candidate will represent the values of the University and the respective department. Examples of fit questions include: For a department that experiences constant change: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new skill or process. How did you handle it? What were your frustrations? For a position that has to make decisions without guidance: Often times we do not have all the information we would like, but still have to make a decision: tell me how you handle these situations. Give some examples and explain if you would handle them differently. 7. All structured interview questions should be identical for each applicant; however it is always acceptable to ask the candidate questions regarding the material they submitted. Common examples include: I see from your application and resume you do not list any work history between 2006 and 2010 can you explain? (The answer to this may return personal information such as “I was a stay at home mom or I had to care for my ill mother.” This is okay however you should not ask further questions.) Your application indicates you supervised 4 employees while at the Acme organization. Your job title there was ‘worker bee’. Can you explain? You indicate you left your first job to make more money. Your second job was a lower salary. Can you explain? In your cover letter you say you have experience with budgets. Can you tell me which job you were working when you gained that experience? I see in your last three jobs your salary was over $60,000. This job has an annual salary of $40,000. Are you aware of this? In your previous positions you held a supervisory role. This job will not supervise others. Are you aware of this? Do you feel you will be comfortable in this role? [Top of Page] Structuring the Interview 1. Before scheduling interviews with the candidate pool, the structure of the interview should be developed. Having a plan for the interview process itself will help ensure that the process flows smoothly and that you use the time with the candidate in the best way possible. 2. To start the planning process, determine where the interview will be held. Is the location inviting? Does it have all of the technical requirements needed for your interview process? Is it easily accessible? Is it handicap accessible? 3. What will the seating arrangements be during the interview? Will the search committee and candidate sit around a table in more informal setting? Or will the interview be “panel style”, with the candidate on one side of the table and the search team on the other? Keep in mind that the setting of the interview can either help put the candidate at ease, or cause stress for the candidate. Whenever possible, always aim to put the candidate at ease. This will help build rapport during the process, which typically leads to a more comfortable experience for both the candidate and the search team members. If using phone interviews, make sure that the location is quiet enough not to disrupt being able to effectively communicate with the candidate. Before the interview, the search chair should discuss the expectations of the search team. Appropriate dress and assignment of the candidate introduction process should be discussed. Also, search team members should know in advance which questions they will be responsible for asking. 4. What will you do to get the interview started once the initial introductions are complete? Many search teams use “ice breaker” activities to start the free flow of information from the candidate. Samples of appropriate questions include: Thank you for coming in today – did you have any problems finding our office? Tell me - Why are you interested in working for Wichita State? What is it about this position that led you to submit your application? Always offer the candidate water or other beverages when available. Interviews are stressful. This action alone can be another type of “icebreaker”. Feel free to contact your assigned HR representative for additional creative suggestions. 5. What activities will the candidate complete? Will there be a campus tour? Will a presentation be required? Will there be any type of testing or writing requirement? Will role plays be a part of the process? All of these things should be considered during interview planning. Appropriate resources should be located and available to the candidate for the required activities. When using activities, make sure that instructions for them are clear, and that each search team member knows what part they will play in the activity. When applicable, desired outcomes for the activities should also be identified beforehand. Feel free to contact your assigned HR representative for additional suggestions. 6. Once the structure and format of the interview has been established, the interviews can then be scheduled with the approved candidates. During the process, the following should be covered: Location, duration and time of the interview. Include any information that could be an issue for the candidate, such as traffic or parking. Who the candidate will be meeting with. This does not mean giving out names, but can be more general in nature. For example, you could tell the candidate “You will be meeting with the search team for the position, which is made up of 4 team members from the department”. Give the candidate information concerning anything that needs to be developed for the interview, such as a portfolio sample or presentation. Provide the candidate with contact information in case they have follow-up questions or they are unable to keep their scheduled interview time. [Top of Page] Conducting Multiple Interviews 1. As you work through the interview process, you may find that you need to interview candidates multiple times to determine who ultimately is the best fit for your position. 2nd or 3rd interviews are considered an acceptable part of the recruiting process and should be used when needed to accurately compare and contrast candidate qualifications. 2. All notes and documentation related to the search should be kept in accordance with Policy 20.23 . [Top of Page] For specific information on Faculty searches, please contact the Office of Academic Affairs. [Top of Page] Revised: 04/23/25 NH

title: Job Offer
text: Job Offer - Job Offer and Offer Letter – Non Teaching Positions After you have completed reference checks, you are ready to begin the offer process. The search chair requests that a contingent offer be extended to a selected candidate using PeopleAdmin. In PeopleAdmin, open posting and go to Applicants tab. Click the check box beside the desired candidate. Click the Actions button and then Move in Workflow. Select Extend Contingent Offer. Search chair receives an email with the link to the Candidate Offer Worksheet. Search chair completes Worksheet and sends it to HR by using the Send button. HR is notified of the offer request through PeopleAdmin. NOTE: Candidate must start work in position at the beginning of a payperiod. HR prepares the offer for the candidate based on the completed Candidate Offer Worksheet. It also includes a review of the following: Verification of the candidate meeting minimum experience and education. Check rehire status if applicable. Check prior state service if applicable. Verification that offer is within the salary structure for the position. Verification that start date is valid NEO date. Verification of need for background check. Verification of need for Driver’s License check based on PD. HR contacts search chair to review the offer details. Search chair emails signed background check release form to HR . HR extends contingent offer to candidate. If candidate declines, HR contacts search chair. If candidate accepts, HR notifies search chair via PeopleAdmin of acceptance. HR sends background check link to candidate (if needed) and starts hiring proposal (HP), including the data entry. The HP will be routed to the budget officer or ORTT Payroll, depending on funding status. HR disqualifies all remaining candidates once the background check is clear. If no background check is required, HR disqualifies all remaining candidates upon offer acceptance. This process will send an email to candidates not selected about the status of the position. When all hiring activities are complete (background check, hiring proposal, etc.), search chair receives an email from HR indicating that the new hire is clear to begin work. NOTE: The candidate cannot begin work in the new position until the email referenced in Step 9 is received indicating that the hiring process is complete. title: Search Team
text: Search Team - The Search Committee is comprised of at least one (1) Search Chair and one (1) or more Search Committee Members. A Search Committee must have at least one Search Chair, but there can be more than one. The Search Chair and Search Committee are selected by the Hiring Manager. Search Committee members are required to participate in all steps of the search. Any member who is unable to participate as required, must recuse themselves from that step of the process. The Search Committee is able to review applicants in the applicant tracking system once a position is posted. Once a position is posted, only Human Resources (HR) can substitute, add or remove members of the Search Committee, if changes need to be made. Search Chair Responsibilities: The Search Chair should be distinguished in her/his department and the university, who has participated in searches resulting in successful recruitment of candidates. The Search Chair will work closely with the Hiring Manager to conduct the search for an optimum outcome. The Search Chair and the Hiring Manager may be the same person. Complete the search in a compliant manner. Complete all hiring process documentation. Save and maintain search file documentation for three (3) years, in case of a legal challenge or federal audit. This includes all notes compiled by committee members. Coordinate with the Hiring Manager to evaluate candidates. Arrange interviews with the candidates and the Search Committee. Search Committee Member Responsibilities: Following the guidelines set by the Search Chair and Hiring Manager Arranging your schedule to accommodate interviews Providing constructive feedback to help determine the optimum hire Keeping detailed records of candidate interactions Remaining flexible to the needs of the committee Revised: 07/18/25 NH
