title: Staff Senate Awards
text: Staff Senate Awards - President's Distinguished Service Award and Staff Excellence Awards The University Staff Senate invites the Wichita State University community to submit nominations for outstanding University Staff for the 2026 President’s Award for Distinguished Service and the newly established Staff Excellence Awards. These awards recognize the dedication and excellence of Wichita State University Staff who have provided exemplary, dedicated and caring service to the WSU community that is beyond the expectations of the duties and responsibilities of their position. Selected honorees are recognized at the annual Shocker Pride Celebration. Nominations can be submitted by anyone from within the Wichita State University community. Nomination materials must be received by 5:00 pm CST on Friday, February 6, 2026. Please send nomination electronically to Gabriel Fonseca at gabriel.fonseca@wichita.edu 2026 Nomination Form 2026 Awards Timeline November 10, 2025 - February 6, 2026: Nominations are open. February 2026: Nominations are reviewed by Awards Committee and President. March 2026: Awards winners for Distinguished Service Award will receive notification of their award. Nominees for Staff Senate Awards will will receive their notification of nomination and invitation to Shocker STRIVE conference. April 2026: Award winners for the Distinguished Service Award are recognized at the Shocker Pride Celebration. President's Distinguished Service Award Each year the University Staff Senate complete a call for nominations among their constituents. Members of each senate award committee select three individuals who have demonstrated outstanding service to the university community beyond their job descriptions. Honorees selected by each Senate are recognized at the Shocker Pride Celebration. Eligibility for the President’s Distinguished Service Award Nominees must be a permanent Wichita State University employee, with at least a .5 appointment and minimum of 1 year of service at WSU. Nominee must exemplify one or more of the following characteristics: Distinguished service to the University Distinguished service to the community Notable outreach efforts and/or forging of connection between WSU and the community Long-term commitment to WSU through extensive committee service Nominees considered for the President’s Distinguished Service Award and Staff Excellence Awards shall only be Unclassified Professional and University Support Staff who are in staff roles at Wichita State University defined as all half-time (0.5 FTE) or greater, exempt, and nonexempt personnel who have an appointment status of contingent, provisional, hourly, or regular. All nominees must have a minimum of 1 year of service at WSU. Staff Excellence Awards Recognizing and celebrating the hard work and dedication of staff members at Wichita State University is essential to building a positive and engaged work environment. The Staff Excellence Awards aims to honor the outstanding contributions, leadership, and service of staff members at Wichita State University who go above and beyond in their roles. These awards will provide an opportunity to highlight the impact that staff have on the University’s success and to foster a culture of appreciation and motivation. Eligibility for the Staff Excellence Awards Nominees must be a permanent Wichita State University employee, with at least a .5 appointment Nominee must exemplify characteristics that pertain to each award. Nominees considered for the President’s Distinguished Service Award and Staff Excellence Awards shall only be Unclassified Professional and University Support Staff who are in staff roles at Wichita State University defined as all half-time (0.5 FTE) or greater, exempt, and nonexempt personnel who have an appointment status of contingent, provisional, hourly, or regular. All nominees must have a minimum of 1 year of service at WSU. The Staff Excellence in Belonging Award The Staff Excellence in Belonging Award is presented to a staff member at Wichita State who prioritizes outstanding work on advancing belonging and inclusiveness to campus amongst staff members. The Staff Excellence in Engagement Award Staff Excellence in Engagement Award is an honor bestowed to an individual staff member who prioritizes engagement. The recipient is recognized for their commitment to building relationships with stakeholders and creating opportunities for partnerships that make a lasting impact. The Staff Excellence in Customer Service Award Staff Excellence in Customer Service Award is an honor bestowed to an individual staff member who prioritizes customer service. The recipient is recognized for their commitment to providing exceptional customer service to internal and external customers of the University. The Young Professional Award The Young Professional Award recognizes emerging leaders at Wichita State University who have demonstrated exceptional professional achievement, leadership, and commitment to the institution’s mission. This award celebrates individuals in the early stages of their careers who, through their contributions, have made a significant impact on their department, students, colleagues, or the broader university community. Nominees should have less than 5 years of professional experience The Everyday Hero Award The Everyday Hero Award is presented to a staff member at Wichita State University who goes above and beyond to help others on campus. This award recognizes a staff member who offers support to a colleague, assisting others, or solves unexpected challenges. This award celebrates those who are always ready to lend a hand and demonstrate extraordinary commitment to teamwork, kindness, and problem-solving. The Staff Excellence in Applied Learning Award The Staff Excellence in Applied Learning Award honors staff members who demonstrate outstanding commitment to student learning beyond the classroom. Recipients of this award actively support, facilitate, or create applied learning experiences that enhance student development, career readiness, and real-world engagement. Their contributions reflect innovation, collaboration, and a deep dedication to student success. The Staff Excellence in Administrative Support Award The Staff Excellence in Administrative Support Award recognizes staff members who provide exceptional administrative service that enhances the efficiency, effectiveness, and overall success of their department or unit. Honorees demonstrate outstanding organizational skills, attention to detail, professionalism, and a commitment to supporting colleagues and institutional goals. Wayne Carlisle Distinguished Service Award One of the WSU Staff awardees selected will be given the exclusive honor of the Wayne Carlisle Distinguished Service Award. The Carlisle Award is presented to an WSU employee who models the standard of extraordinary service exhibited by the late Wayne Carlisle. More Information about Wayne Carlisle

title: Staff Senate Merger
text: Staff Senate Merger - Introduction In 2017, the Unclassified Professional (UP) Senate and University Support Staff (USS) Senate began having a conversation about the potential of merging the two Senates into one body, representing the thousands of staff members on campus. In 2019, the Senate approved a three-year priority plan which included bringing forth a formal recommendation to the Senates. Current Representation Proposed Representation UP: 15 Senators, 4 At-Large Senators Apportioned by division USS: 11 Senators Previously apportioned by job classification University Staff Senate: 24 Senators, 6 At-Large Senators Apportioned between exempt and non-exempt staff Senate Executive Committee must contain at least one UP and one USS employee Addition of Vice President role Benefits New Representation Format: Senate representation would be made up of eligible exempt (salaried) and non-exempt (hourly) staff. Currently, 47% of staff are exempt and 53% are non-exempt. A Collective Voice: Uniting as one senate will make our collective voices strong, allowing us to better represent and advocate for all staff. As USS positions have been vacated in recent years, they have been moved to UP positions causing the number of USS to shrink over time to approximately 250 positions. This decline in USS positions has presented challenges in obtaining a full slate of senators for the current USS Senate. Efficiency: For the last two years, the UP and USS Senates have been holding joint monthly meetings and have combined nearly all of our committees. Both senate presidents attend meetings together with the university president, human resources, and others. A joint Senate enables staff leaders to be more efficient with their time and University resources. Preserving Leadership Representation: The new constitution would require a USS/UP representative be elected to serve on the University Staff Senate executive committee so both groups will continue to have a voice on the leadership team. For example, if the elected senate president was a USS employee, a UP representative would be elected to the executive committee and vice versa. This joint representation will allow us to serve as a voice and better advocate for all staff without duplicating efforts. Proposed Constitution If the merger is approved, the new Wichita State University Staff Senate would operate according to the new constitution below. The Constitution of the Wichita State University Staff Senate would replace both the UP and USS Constitutions that currently exist. For your convenience, the proposed constitution, as well as the two old constitutions are provided below. NEW: Constitution of the Wichita State University Staff Senate CURRENT: UP Constitution CURRENT: USS Constitution Timeline September 28-29, 2020: The UP and USS Senates held listening sessions this fall to discuss with staff the idea of merging our Senates into one. We received a lot of great feedback and ideas that were used to develop the proposed Constitution of the Wichita State University Staff Senate. October 20, 2020: The combined UP and USS Organizational Committee prepared a recommendation taking into consideration the feedback from the listening sessions. November 17, 2020: The Organizational Committee presented the recommendation at the combined Senate meeting. Each senate voted in support of the new constitution and merging to become the University Staff Senate. December 9, 2020: The new constitution will be presented to the staff at the Fall General Meeting on Wednesday, December 9 from 10-11:30 a.m. Following the meeting all UP and USS staff will be sent a link to cast their vote electronically. December 16, 2020: The Unclassified Professional Staff and University Support Staff voted in support of merging the UP and USS Senates and adopting the constitution of the University Staff Senate. July 1, 2021: The two Senates will officially merge to become the University Staff Senate. FAQs How will it be determined if the new Constitution passes? In order for the new Constitution to pass, both constituency groups (UP and USS) must receive a majority of "yes" votes. If passed, when will the Senates officially merge? The proposed merger would occur on July 1, 2021. Details for the transition/election of returning/incoming senators are still being discussed. Why are the Senates moving away from divisional representation? In recent years, both Senates have struggled to find representation (eligible and willing-to-serve senators) for some divisions and/or job classifiications. Additionally, when reviewing policy changes/recommendations for the University, the most common alignment for shared experiences seemed to be along the lines of exempt (salaried) and non-exempt (hourly) staff. Moreover, divisions are often fluid at the University and have been adapting to the changing structures in higher education in recent years - each time the divisions shift, the representation of senators has needed to adjust. What are the benefits of apportioning representation by exempt and non-exempt staff? Being represented by a fellow staff member who is more likely to have shared experiences in their employment relationship with the University is key to ensuring staff voices are understood and heard both in the Senate and to University administration. As many policies at the University affect exempt and non-exempt employees differently, the proposed Constitution acknowledges this experience and offers the opportunity to ensure a broader staff representation than the old divisional-based format. I'm a USS employee, will I still have a voice? Yes. While you will no longer elect senators based on USS or UP classification, you will still be represented by fellow employees (exempt or non-exempt) who may have shared employment experiences. Additionally, the proposed Constitution ensures at least one USS representative is appointed to the University Staff Senate executive team. This individual would serve on the executive team and represent all USS voices on the statewide Kansas Board of Regents (KBOR) USS Senate Council. I'm a UP employee, will I still have a voice? Yes. While you will no longer elect senators based on USS or UP classification, you will still be represented by fellow employees (exempt or non-exempt) who may have shared employment experiences. Additionally, the proposed Constitution ensures at least one UP representative is appointed to the University Staff Senate executive team. This individual would serve on the executive team and represent all UP voices on the statewide Kansas Board of Regents (KBOR) UP Senate Council. Other questions? Please reach out to your Senator or to the Senate Presidents. USS Senate President: Randy Sessions UP Senate President: Trish Gandu

title: About Staff Senate
text: About Staff Senate - University Staff Senate Purpose The purpose of the organization is to foster communication and collegiality among staff at Wichita State University, and to Provide representation for Unclassified Professional (UP) and University Support Staff (USS) personnel and liaison to the University administration and others regarding issues of concern; Initiate and review policies and procedures relating to UP and USS personnel; Be a cultural driver for WSU staff that reflects the values of Wichita State University’s Strategic Plan. Membership of the Senate The Senate consists of: Twenty-four (24) members, elected by the electorate, split between exempt and non-exempt staff Six (6) at-large members, appointed by the President; split between exempt and non-exempt staff and approved by the Senate The President of the University, the President of the Faculty Senate, and the President of the Student Government Association are ex officio, non-voting members of the Senate. A representative from the Wichita State University Foundation, Wichita State University Intercollegiate Athletic Association, Inc., Wichita State University Union Corporation and the Wichita State University Alumni Association ex officio non-voting members of the Senate. Activities of the Senate Sponsors a minimum of two general meetings of all Unclassified Professional personnel (one each in the spring and fall semesters) to report publicly on issues that have come before the senate, share actions they have taken, and solicit feedback on issues of concern to the entire constituency. Oversees activities of a number of committees, including Elections, Service, Communication, and Awards and Recognition. Appoints representatives to various University-level committees; studies issues and makes recommendations to the President and Vice-Presidents; and organizes support for University initiatives. Maintains a Web page at wichita.edu/staffsenate Maintains and distributes information to WSU staff, including announcements regarding events, current policies, and issues of concern to staff at Wichita State University. Comments or Concerns? Provide feedback to the Staff Senate here: Senate Feedback Form As of August 5, 2021

title: Wayne Carlisle
text: Wayne Carlisle - Wayne Carlise Wayne served as the Director of Placement and Career Services for eight years. Colleagues say Carlisle managed a multitude of tasks each day with intelligence, warmth, courage, and humor. During his career at Wichita State he helped to bring thousands of students and alumni together with prospective employers. Carlisle also was founding member of the WSU Research Group on Women and Work. Since 1985 he helped collect, analyze and present data on two comprehensive surveys of working women. In 1990, the National Association of Student Personnel Administrators (NASPA) presented him with the Fred Turner Award for service, one of the organization’s most prestigious awards. Mr. Carlisle earned the respect of his peers not only for his professional success, but also for the courageous battle he waged against cancer. That fight led to his retirement on Dec. 4 th , with him passing on Dec. 17 th , 1991.

title: Staff Senate Professional Development Conference
text: Staff Senate Professional Development Conference - Shocker Strive Conference Friday, March 27, 2026 • Rhatigan Student Center Registration is closed for the 2026 Conference. Feel free to reach out to shockerstrive@wichita.edu with any questions. The Third Annual Staff Trainings Resources Initiatives Values and Engagement (STRIVE) conference, established in 2024, offers all WSU staff a free professional development opportunity and a chance to network with fellow Shockers within the Wichita State University community. The Staff Senate aims to create a flexible opportunity for any interested staff to attend, learn, and connect with others. To accommodate various schedules, we offer both morning and afternoon sessions. There will be a morning welcome message at 8:15 am and an afternoon welcome message at 12:30 pm. For those attending, box lunches will be available for those who are registered to attend the event from Noon to 1 p.m. During the lunch hour, we will host an awards ceremony to celebrate those honored with Staff Senate awards as well! During the event, Staff Senators will also be available in black shirts all day, please ask these representatives if you need any assistance or have any feedback. Thank you to President Rick Muma, Provost Monica Lounsbery and David Miller for helping sponsor the Shocker Strive Conference. Morning Sessions 8:30 to 9:30am Docking Survey Session Overview: This session will provide an overview of the Docking Survey results that were presented to Staff Senate. Presenters will highlight key findings, common themes that emerged from staff feedback, and the initial recommendations developed in response to the data. The session will also focus on the importance of gathering broader campus input to ensure that next steps are thoughtful, collaborative, and responsive to staff needs. Participants will have the opportunity to learn about the process used to review the survey results and to share feedback that can help inform future actions and implementation efforts. Presenters: Gabriel Fonseca, Jacob Mendez Location: RSC Beggs Ballroom CARE Team Confessions: What We Can Tell You… and What We Really, Really Can’t Session Overview: Faculty and staff often encounter students who are distressed, overwhelmed, or unsure where to turn for help—and many campus partners play a role in supporting them. But not every office is bound by the same laws or able to share information in the same ways. In this session, the Directors of Student Outreach & Support (SOS), Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS), and Student Health Services (SHS) will demystify the differences between FERPA and HIPAA and explain how these regulations shape what information can be shared, with whom, and under what circumstances. This session will walk you through scenarios, questions we're often asked, and allow ample time for Q&A with the presenters. Attendees will leave with concrete tools and campus‑wide resources that can be used to support students—and themselves—in difficult moments. Presenters: Katie Davidson, Chris Leonard, Heather Stafford Location: RSC 266 The Employment Landscape: What Today’s Hiring Trends Mean for WSU Students Session Overview: You know all about it, workforce needs are changing quickly, but are employer recruitment strategies changing too? This session outlines what Career Services professionals are seeing on the ground working with corporate partners, common pitfalls for students, what that means for students post graduation outcomes, and how YOU can impact their success. Participants will gain insight into how WSU staff can help students build confidence, articulate their strengths, and navigate an evolving recruitment landscape. Presenters: Brian Austin Location: RSC 265 9:45 to 10:45 a.m. Role of the Leader Session Overview: Forget the org chart. Real management happens in the moments between meetings, in the decisions made under pressure, and in the relationships that hold teams together. In this one-hour session, we explore Henry Mintzberg's landmark framework for understanding what managers actually do and why it still matters decades after it was first introduced. Through his three core role categories (Interpersonal, Informational, and Decisional) Mintzberg cuts through management theory to reveal the ten distinct roles every effective supervisor plays. Whether you're new to supervision or a seasoned leader looking to sharpen your self-awareness, this session offers a practical lens for reflecting on your own management style, identifying your strengths, and recognizing where you may have blind spots. You'll leave with a clearer picture of the full scope of the managerial role and a new vocabulary for talking about the work you do every day. Presenters: Raina Rutti, Chris Stone Location: RSC 266 Putting the U in stUdent sUccess! Session Overview: Join us to learn about university persistence/retention tools, campus resources, and simple strategies you can put into practice to help students feel more connected and supported at Wichita State. Presenters: Kim Sandlin Location: RSC 265 Belonging with Purpose Session Overview: Belonging with Purpose invites staff to think about what it really means to help others feel they matter, while still honoring the expectations and boundaries of our institution. Together, we’ll talk through approachable ways to build meaningful connections, support a wide range of experiences, and strengthen trust across our community. This session offers practical tools for handling tricky moments with confidence and intention, all while contributing to a campus environment where students and colleagues alike feel valued, supported, and able to thrive. Presenters: Gabriel Fonseca Location: RSC 233 11 a.m. to Noon Getting to know Generative AI at WSU Session Overview: Find out about current Generative AI efforts going on at WSU; What can you use and how can you use it safely? What impact does it have? What are others doing around campus? Presenters: John Jones Location: RSC 266 Finance 101 Session Overview: Finance 101 is designed for anyone who processes invoices, enters requisitions, monitors budgets, or has financial questions at WSU. It provides a simplified introduction to fund types, the FOAPAL structure, the annual budget cycle, key financial systems such as TM1, Emburse Enterprise, Wu‑Buy, and Banner Self Service 9, and the essential reports used to track departmental budgets and transactions. Presenters: Kristie Courtney, Lyndsay Pletcher Location: RSC 233 Putting Strengths to Work: How to Collaborate Across Different Talents Session Overview: This interactive session will focus on identifying unique strengths and contributions to the workplace. Participants will discuss their talents and how they leverage them personally and professionally. title: Staff Senate Scholarship
text: Staff Senate Scholarship - University Staff Senate Scholarship Staff and Dependents Tuition & Fee Scholarship The University Staff Senate is committed to helping staff members grow and improve their work skills and knowledge at Wichita State University. By offering this scholarship it builds employee confidence, increases job competency, expands access to industry professionals, and enhances potential for career growth. Applications & Timelines Fall Scholarship application: Due February 1 Spring Scholarship application: Due November 1 Awardees will be notified within 2 months of application deadline. Scholarship Application One Time Donation to the Scholarship Payroll Deduction Form Fall 2025 Awards Spring 2026 Awards Fall 2026 Awards Purpose The University Staff Senate Scholarship: Staff and Dependents Tuition & Fee Scholarship has been established with contributions to the Wichita State University Foundation and is sponsored by The University Staff Senate of Wichita State University (WSU). The goal in establishing this scholarship is to help in the advancement of WSU employees and their dependents. The University Staff Senate feels by establishing a scholarship for WSU employees/dependents they are encouraging employees/dependents to start or continue toward a bachelor’s degree at Wichita State University. Appropriate Use of Funds Tuition Books Fees Award Size Scholarship awards are dependent on fund availability. The maximum amount per award is set at $1,000.00 , with typical awards of $250.00-$500.00 per semester, per person. Definitions Benefit-eligible staff employee: a staff member holding a 0.5 FTE or greater position at the University, as an unclassified professional employee or a university support staff. Dependent children: natural, step, or adopted children of a University Benefit-eligible employee, under the age of 26, and who are unmarried. Eligibility & Application Requirements Must be fully admitted to a degree-seeking undergraduate academic program at the University. Must be pursuing your first bachelor's degree. Complete the application which includes an area to upload the following: An unofficial transcript High school graduated, community college, or WSU. An essay The essay should include a brief overview of your contributions to the Wichita community at large and your personal long-range goals. It should also highlight why you deserve the scholarship and how you anticipate using your degree. title: Wichita State University Unclassified Professional Senate Constitution
text: Wichita State University Unclassified Professional Senate Constitution - Wichita State University Unclassified Professional Senate Constitution Approved by the Unclassified Professional Personnel November 17, 1992 Approved by President Warren B. Armstrong March 16, 1993 Revised, May 2, 1996 Revised, June 22, 2010 Revised, May 1, 2014 Revised, February 14, 2017 Article I Name : The name of the organization shall be the Unclassified Professional Senate of Wichita State University. Vision For Up Senate : UP Senate is recognized as the voice of the unclassified professional within the WSU community. Mission Statement : The mission of the UP Senate is to empower and support unclassified professionals in creating a campus culture that fulfills the vision and mission of the WSU community Article II: Purpose The purpose of the organization is to foster communication and collegiality among Unclassified Professional personnel of the University, and to: Provide representation for Unclassified Professional personnel and liaison to the University administration and others regarding issues of concern; Initiate and review policies and procedures relating to Unclassified Professional personnel; Be a cultural driver for Unclassified Professionals that reflects the values of Wichita State University's Strategic Plan. Article III: Membership Section 1. Eligibility for Membership. The membership shall consist of all State of Kansas Unclassified Professional personnel at Wichita State University defined as all half-time (0.5 FTE) or greater, exempt and non-exempt personnel who have an appointment status of emergency, temporary, seasonal, contingent, provisional, hourly, or regular. Executive administrators and members of the President's Executive Team are ineligible for the Unclassified Professional Senate electorate. Executive administrators and members of the President's Executive Team include, but are not limited to, those persons holding the title, or interim title, of President, Vice President, Associate Vice President, Assistant Vice President, and Dean. Section 2. Composition. The membership of the Senate shall consist of: Fifteen members elected by the Unclassified Professional electorate; and Four at-large members appointed by the Senate. Ex-officio members: In order to be inclusive of the University community, each of the following affiliated/or related organizations shall be invited to appoint a representative. Such organizations presently include; WSU Foundation, WSU Intercollegiate Athletic Association, Inc., WSU Union Corporation and the WSU Alumni Association. Section 3. Representation. Fifteen Senators shall be elected from the divisions of the University. The apportionment of elected Senators to the divisions of the University shall be determined by the Election Committee on the basis of the number of Unclassified Professional personnel appointed to each division as of the 20th day of class each spring semester. Each division shall have a minimum of one elected Senator. At the first meeting following the Senatorial election, the standing Senate shall appoint four at-large Senators from a slate recommended by the Election Committee to enhance the Senate's diversity and expertise. Section 4. Terms of Membership. Terms of membership shall be two years beginning July 1 following each annual election. After serving two consecutive terms, a Senator shall not be eligible for re-election for one senate year. A Senator who leaves the division from which elected shall continue to serve in the Senate until the next regularly scheduled election, at which time his/her position will be refilled by a representative from the original division. All officers are exempt from term limits for the term of their appointment. A vacancy on the Senate shall be filled by a majority vote of the remaining Senate. The term of the appointment will be until the next regularly scheduled election. Being appointed to the Senate to fill an unexpired term has no impact on that person's eligibility for serving two consecutive elected terms. To insure continuity, approximately one-half of the Senate shall be elected each year. If the immediate past President is completing the second year of his/her second term, he/she will serve one additional year as an ex-officio member, in order to lend continuity to the governing body. Section 5. Voting Privileges. Each elected Senator and the four at-large members shall have one vote. The Senate President and ex-officio members shall not have voting privileges. However, in the event a deciding vote is required, the Senate President will provide the deciding vote. Senator must be present to cast their vote. A Senator cannot send a proxy to vote in their absence. In the event that an issue arises where input from the Unclassified Professional Senate is needed prior to a normally scheduled meeting, and with the agreement of the Senators, the President of the Senate shall conduct an emergency vote via electronic means as follows: The issue shall be presented to the Senators and approval sought for an electronic vote. If the Senators approve of handling the issue via electronic means then standard protocol shall be followed in regards to the issue as if it were being handled during a regular Senate meeting including: Discussion of the topic, a motion, a second, and then a vote. Article IV: Elections Section 1. Electorate. The electorate shall consist of all State of Kansas Unclassified Professional personnel at Wichita State University defined as all half-time (0.5 FTE) or greater, exempt and non-exempt personnel who have an appointment status of emergency, temporary, seasonal, contingent, provisional, hourly, or regular. Executive administrators and members of the President's Executive Team are ineligible for the Unclassified Professional Senate electorate. Executive administrators and members of the President's Executive Team include, but are not limited to, those persons holding the title, or interim title, of President, Vice President, Associate Vice President, Assistant Vice President, and Dean. Section 2. Election Committee. The Election Committee shall consist of two members: The Election Chair shall have served as Co-Chair prior to becoming Chair. The Co-Chair shall have two years left in their term so they will be able to serve as Chair for at least one year prior to the end of their term. In the event that the Chair's term is ending and the Co-Chair is unable to fulfill the duties of the Chair an Election Chair and new Co-Chair shall be nominated from current senators. Appointments to the election committee shall be made annually and shall be balanced between one and two-year memberships. Section 3. Senatorial Election Procedures. On the 20 th day of class of the spring semester, the Election Committee shall obtain a list of the electorate. The Election Committee shall solicit nominations for Senators from the electorate within each division. The nominations may be by peer or self. All nominations received shall be placed on the appropriate ballot unless a nominee declines to run. A ballot shall be constructed for each division and sent to the divisional electorate. The candidate(s) receiving the most votes in each divisional election shall be considered elected. Ties shall be decided, in order of sequence, by: (1) either candidate conceding to the other candidate, (2) the Senate using the tie vote to fill an at large position, or (3) a second ballot. (4) In the event of a repeated tie the two candidates' names shall be brought before the Senate and the Senators shall vote to determine who will fill the seat. Section 4. Election Timelines. The ballots shall be distributed to the electorate no later than April 1. The results shall be announced no later than May 1 after the election. Section 5. Recall Elections. Justification for Recall Reasons for initiating recall action against a Senator include dereliction of duty, malfeasance, or unethical conduct in the performance of Senatorial responsibilities. Elected Senators An elected Senator shall be subject to recall upon presentation to the Election Committee of a petition signed by 25% or 25 members of the electorate from that Senator's division, whichever is the smaller number. Verification of the signatories as valid members of the electorate shall be made by the Election Committee using official university appointment records. Verification of the number of Unclassified Professional personnel necessary to constitute 25% of the electorate from the division in question shall be made by the Election Committee using the number of Unclassified Professional personnel as determined on the previous 20th day of class of the spring semester. After verification of the validity of the petition, the Election Committee shall hold a divisional ballot to determine whether the Senator shall be recalled. The question of recall shall be determined by majority vote of the divisional electorate participating in the ballot. Appointed Senators Appointed Senators shall be subject to recall upon presentation to the Election Committee of a petition signed by 25 members of the general electorate. Verification of the signatories as valid members of the general electorate shall be made by the Election Committee using official university appointment records. After verification of the validity of the petition, the Election Committee shall hold a general ballot to determine whether the Senator shall be recalled. The question of recall shall be determined by a majority vote of the general electorate participating in the ballot. Section 6. Special Elections. The Election Committee shall conduct special elections as the nature of the vacancy warrants. Article V: Organization Of The Senate Section 1. Officers. Officers of the Senate shall be the President, Vice President (President Elect), and the Secretary. Section 2. Election of Officers. The Vice President shall be elected, by the Senate members, and assume office as the Vice President at the first Senate meeting of the Senate year. The Vice President, as the incoming President, shall assume office following the last meeting of the Senate year. The Secretary shall be elected, by the Senate members, at the first Senate meeting of the Senate Year, and shall serve for twelve (12) months. Section 3. Meetings. The Senate year shall be defined as July 1 through June 30. Meetings shall be scheduled according to need and held no less than twice a semester. The time and place of Senate meetings shall be set by the Senate. Regular Senate meetings shall be open to members of the university community. Upon concurrence of a majority of Senators attending a meeting, the Senate may enter into Executive Session for discussion of privileged items. Only Senators shall attend Executive Sessions. Only the fifteen elected and four at-large Senators may vote at Senate meetings. Section 4. Quorum. Eleven voting members of the Senate shall constitute a quorum. Section 5. Special Meetings. Special meetings of the Senate can be called by the President of the Senate. Special meetings of the Senate can be called upon written request of five Senators to the President or Vice President of the Senate. a. Special meetings shall be held within ten working days of receipt of the written request. Section 6. Rules of Order. The Senate shall determine its own rules of procedure, including time and place of meetings and the form of reports. Section 7. Senate Agenda. Agendas for Senate meetings shall be set by the Senate officers. Additional items may be added to the agenda upon request of one or more Senators. Section 8. Attendance. Senators unable to attend Senate meetings are to notify the President in advance. Excessive absences, as determined by the Senate, may result in the replacement of a Senator. A majority vote of the Senate is required for removal of a Senator. Elected Senators are expected to personally attend meetings and cannot send representatives or proxies. Article VI: Officers Section 1. Duties of Officers. Officers of the Senate and their duties are: President. The President shall be the official spokesperson for, and preside at all meetings of the Senate. The President shall preside at general meetings of the Unclassified Professional personnel. The President shall serve as ex-officio member of all Senate committees except the Election Committee. The President, in cooperation with the other officers, shall establish the agenda for Senate meetings. The President shall represent the UP in meetings with the President of the university. The President shall serve no more than two consecutive one-year terms. Vice President. The Vice President shall serve in the absence of the President, and in case of resignation of the President, shall assume the duties of the President. The Vice President shall serve no more than two consecutive one-year terms. Secretary. The Secretary shall maintain the records of the Senate and record and distribute the minutes of Senate meetings and general meetings. The Secretary shall coordinate Senate correspondence. The Secretary shall preside at meetings in the absence of the President and the Vice President. The Secretary shall serve no more than two consecutive one-year terms. Section 2. Removal of Officers. Officers may be removed during the term of office for reasons of dereliction of duty, malfeasance, or unethical conduct in the performance of the responsibilities of office. Removal of an officer from office during the course of the annual term shall require a majority vote of the Senate. Article VII: General Meetings Section 1. Regular Meetings. The Unclassified Professional personnel shall meet at least once each fall and spring semester at a time and place specified by the Senate. The time and place of such meetings shall be announced to the Unclassified Professional personnel at least fifteen working days prior to the meeting. Section 2. Special Meetings. Special meetings may be held at any time upon: the call of the President of the Senate; the call of the Senate; the request of at least 25 members of the electorate, presented to the President or Vice President in writing, stating the object of the desired meeting; or the request of the University President. See also Article V, Section 5. Special Meetings . Section 3. Quorum. A quorum shall be those present and voting. Section 4. Agenda. Agendas for general meetings shall be set by the Senate. Additional items may be added to the agenda upon request in writing by ten members of the electorate. Requests for addition of agenda items shall be submitted to the Secretary of the Senate at least ten working days prior to the meeting. Article VIII: Committees Section 1. Standing Committees. Standing committees shall report to the Senate, which has authority and responsibility for those committees and their membership. Standing committees of the Senate shall include, but not be limited to, the Election Committee, and the Unclassified Professional Grievance Committee. Additional standing committees may be constituted by the Senate as it deems necessary. Membership on the standing committees consist of voting Senators and members of the general electorate. The membership and conduct of standing committees shall be subject to Senate review. If necessary, the Senate shall initiate special action to ensure the appropriate functioning of standing committees; such special action shall require a majority vote of the Senate for approval. Section 2. Ad Hoc Committees and Task Forces. Ad hoc committees and task forces shall report to the Senate, which has authority and responsibility for those bodies and their membership. Ad hoc committees and task forces shall be constituted at the discretion of the Senate or upon written request of 25 members of the electorate to address special issues concerning the constituency. Members of ad hoc committees and task forces shall be appointed by the Senate from the standing Senate or the Unclassified Professional constituency. The term of appointment of ad hoc committees or task forces shall be determined by the Senate. The membership and conduct of ad hoc committees and task forces shall be subject to Senate review. If necessary, the Senate shall initiate special action to ensure the appropriate functioning of ad hoc committees and task forces; such special action shall require a majority vote of the Senate for approval. Section 3. University Committees. The Senate shall recommend to the University President candidates for appointment as Unclassified Professional representatives to University committees. Candidates may be recommended from the Senate or the general constituency. Article IX: Amendments Section 1. Proposed Amendments. Amendments to this Constitution may be proposed by any member of the Senate or by any member of the Unclassified Professional electorate. All proposed amendments shall be placed on the agenda of the next Senate meeting. Section 2. Consideration of Proposed Amendments. If the Senate approves the proposed amendment, it shall be placed on the agenda of the next general meeting. If the amendment was proposed by a member of the Senate or by fewer than 25 members of the electorate, a negative vote by the Senate shall be final. If the amendment was proposed by 25 or more members of the electorate, the proposed amendment together with the Senate recommendation shall be placed on the agenda of the next general meeting, even if the Senate vote is negative. Section 3. Adoption of Amendments. A majority of the electorate participating in the vote shall be required for adoption of the proposed amendment. Article X: Authority of The Senate Section 1. General Meetings. The President of the Senate shall consult with the President of the University regarding the need for general meetings of the Unclassified Professional personnel and shall schedule such meetings appropriately. Section 2. Senate Deliberations. The Senate may deliberate and recommend on all issues committed to it regarding Unclassified Professional personnel at Wichita State University and on any matter of concern to its constituency. Section 3. Committees. The Senate has authority and responsibility for its standing committees, ad hoc committees, and task forces and has responsibility for ensuring the appropriate conduct of those bodies and their membership. Section 4. Senate Action. Action of the Unclassified Professional Senate is final, unless 25 or more members of the electorate request that the issue be placed on the agenda of the next general meeting. Requests for addition of the issue as an agenda item must be presented to the Secretary of the Senate in writing at least ten working days prior to the scheduled meeting. Section 5. Constitution. A copy of the Constitution shall be made available to each Senator and shall be reviewed at the first Senate meeting of each new Senate year. Article XI: Conflict Of Interest Members of the Senate, or members of the constituency serving on standing, ad hoc, or university committees or task forces, shall appropriately absent themselves from participation in any activity or discussion which may be perceived as conflict of interest. Definition Of Terms Ad Hoc Committees and Task Forces refer to ad hoc committees and task forces established by the Unclassified Professional Senate. Amendment refers to any statement that is added to, revises, or improves the constitution. Constituency refers to all persons appointed as Unclassified Professional personnel at Wichita State University. Electorate refers to all State of Kansas Unclassified Professional personnel at Wichita State University defined as all half-time (0.5 FTE) or greater, exempt and non-exempt personnel who have an appointment status of emergency, temporary, seasonal, contingent, provisional, hourly, or regular. Executive administrators and members of the President's Executive Team are ineligible for the Unclassified Professional Senate electorate. Executive administrators and members of the President's Executive Team include, but are not limited to, those persons holding the title, or interim title, of President, Vice President, Associate Vice President, Assistant Vice President, and Dean. Senate refers to the Unclassified Professional Senate created by this Constitution. Senate Year refers to the period of time from July 1 through June 30 of the following calendar year. Standing Committees refer to standing committees established by the Unclassified Professional Senate. University refers to Wichita State University.

I hope to represent WSU within the Senate role and provide outreach to all as we continue to expand and meet the challenges that face us every day. I look forward to this new opportunity and appreciate being nominated. Jairus Joseph I am grateful to have been nominated to serve on the University Staff Senate. I came to Wichita in 2013 to pursue a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and later continued my studies with a Master’s in Computer Networking. I began my career at NIAR as a Graduate Research Assistant (GRA) and transitioned to a full-time position in 2019. I am passionate about advocating for the needs of my colleagues and enhancing the work environment at WSU. Serving on the Staff Senate will allow me to bring forward ideas that positively impact our community and ensure that staff voices are heard in university decision-making. I hope to contribute to creating a supportive and inclusive workplace by addressing staff concerns and working collaboratively to implement solutions that improve our overall work experience and university culture. Sara Mata Greetings! My name is Sara Mata, and I serve as the Executive Director for Hispanic Serving Initiatives. I am deeply honored to be nominated and considered for a position on Staff Senate. Over the past three years, I have dedicated myself to the creation and development of the Office of Hispanic Serving Initiatives. This work has provided me the invaluable opportunity to connect with departments, offices, and staff members across the university. As a practitioner, I strongly believe in fostering a sense of community and collaboration with the various support areas on campus. My approach centers on continuously enhancing and discovering effective ways to serve our students. By joining Staff Senate, I hope to strengthen these connections intentionally and gain a broader understanding of how I can best contribute to both the staff and the university as a whole. I look forward to the opportunity to expand my network, foster collaboration, and work holistically to advance the shared goal of promoting student success. Sarah Mathews My name is Sarah Mathews, and I am the Director for Career Development in the Shocker Career Accelerator. I graduated from WSU with a M.Ed. in Sport Management in 2014 and have worked at Wichita State for over 10 years. I started my career in the Athletic Department in Student Services and Compliance, where I worked for 9 years before transitioning to the Shocker Career Accelerator. I oversee the Career Ready Team. Our team is focused on teaching students the skills to navigate their career journey and to support faculty in integrating career readiness into their classroom. I am interested in participating in the Staff Senate because it allows me to contribute to the decision-making process on matters that affect the university’s staff. Additionally, I look forward to networking with colleagues across departments and helping shape the university’s culture and policies. Cheryl Miller I am the senior assistant dean for Fairmount College and serve as the point of contact for college strategic communication, public relations, college-wide events, staff concerns, and operations. I also serve as college commencement coordinator, and coordinate major college events such as Hall of Fame. I started at Wichita State in 1994 as coordinator of orientation, which was then in student affairs, and began reporting to the Fairmount College dean’s office in 1998. I previously served on the Unclassified Professional Senate and would use this term to communicate concerns I hear from college staff as well as participate in discussions that would improve our work environment. Patricia Morriss Hello! My name is Patricia Morriss, although many of you know me by Mary Morriss. I am grateful to be nominated to serve on Staff Senate. Currently, I work in the Office of Instructional Resources department as an LMS specialist working with both faculty and students who need assistance with Blackboard. I have been with Wichita State University for over 28 years. I started my Career with WSU as the telecourse coordinator and helped grow a successful program of broadcast courses delivered via our Campus Television Channel, Cox cable 13. As the world of media changed, I transitioned to online learning work where I still remain happily. I also teach courses at WSU, and have degrees in English, Philosophy and Religious Studies. I am honored to be nominated. Andrew Myers Hi there. It means a lot to me to be nominated for a position in the University Staff Senate. I am the director of scholarships and student services in the Dorothy and Bill Cohen Honors College. I have worked for Wichita State for a total of 13 years this upcoming summer. However, my career in higher education and education spans nearly 22 years. As you are creating a checklist or an informational email from scratch, do you ever wonder if someone else on campus has already done this and has experienced success? My hope is that we can find ways to work together as a university staff and not as if we are on separate islands when it comes to a process or a system to help an office, event, or program run smoothly. We need a centralized, digitized way of sharing tips, templates, and talent. There are so many talented people working as members of our staff who have tips on successful event planning, successful mail merge templates, or even presentations related to workplace soft skills. With so many unpredictable barriers on the horizon for public universities, we need to be able to rely on each other. Let’s find a way to better share our tips, templates, and talents. I love serving the students at Wichita State. Moreover, I love working at Wichita State. I’m happy to do what I can to serve the staff at Wichita State. What helps us will help serve the students and our community. Chantal Nez Hello! My name is Chantal Nez, and I am honored to be nominated to serve on Staff Senate. I have been with the Community Engagement Institute for over two years, working to strengthen community connections and improve public health initiatives across Kansas. My passion lies in creating a space within Wichita State University where Indigenous students can thrive, feel seen, and feel safe. I believe that when Indigenous students have the support, resources, and community they need, they can use their skills to uplift and serve their Native communities. Additionally, I am committed to working with staff and faculty to foster cultural awareness and respect for Indigenous students on campus, ensuring WSU is a welcoming and inclusive environment for all. I look forward to the opportunity to represent WSU staff and advocate for meaningful change. I am grateful for this nomination and the chance to continue serving our campus community. Kendra Nguyen Hello! My name is Kendra Nguyen, and I’m a Public Health Program Specialist with the Center for Public Health Initiatives at the WSU Community Engagement Institute. I’ve been a part of the WSU community since 2017, and it has been such a rewarding experience to get involved wherever I can. I’ve had the privilege of serving as both a senator and an at-large senator on the Staff Senate, and I’m truly honored to be nominated once again. From a young age, I’ve always loved being engaged, learning, and bringing fresh perspectives to the table. I have a deep curiosity about how things work and why, and I’m passionate about creating spaces where all voices can be heard. Staff Senate has given me a valuable opportunity to understand the bigger picture of our university—how decisions are made and how they impact us as staff. As Senators, we play a crucial role in advocating for our colleagues, sharing their concerns with WSU leadership, and helping shape solutions that enhance our work environment. One of my core commitments is ensuring that those who are often left out of important conversations have a seat at the table. Everyone’s voice matters, and I’m excited to continue working toward a more inclusive and supportive campus for all. Chukwunenye Nweke Hello, my name is Chukwunenye Nweke, most people know me as Chuck. I am one of the mental health counselors at Counseling and Psychological Services. I am grateful for the nomination to serve on the staff senate. I have worked at Wichita State University for almost 3 years. It would be an honor being able to serve on the Staff senate and work towards improving staff recognition and connection. Cora Olson Hello! My name is Cora Olson. I am the Wellness Program and Outreach Manager for the Student Wellness Center and have the privilege of supporting the work of Health, Outreach, Prevention and Education (HOPE) Services, Student Health, and Counseling and Psychological Services. I have been with Wichita State University for nearly seven years, first as a graduate student teaching and conducting research, and now for four years in a full-time staff role focusing on prevention and health promotion. I also serve on the HOPE Services Advisory Board (HSAB) and chair both the Health and Wellness Subcommittee and the Preventing Sexual Violence Subcommittee. Working for the Student Wellness Center, HOPE Services, and with HSAB has given me the opportunity to contribute to positive changes by cultivating a culture of wellness on our campus for our students and our employees. It is an honor to have been nominated to serve on the Staff Senate and I believe that such a role aligns with my current work and passion of equipping the WSU community to continue to grow in health and resiliency. Data suggests that caring for our employees is a pivotal part of caring for our students and campus community therefore, if elected, I will advocate for sustainable growth and increased utilization of existing wellness programs for staff such as the Student Health employee acute care clinic, Suspenders4Hope workplace wellness programming, or the Employee Assistance Program offered through the benefits package. Thank you for considering me as a 2025 Staff Senate nominee. Naquela Pack I’ve been at WSU for about five years, starting at the onset of the pandemic. Adapting through change has deepened my commitment to advocating for staff. I’m running for Staff Senate to bring a fresh perspective and continue my work in improving representation, resources, and opportunities for staff. I look forward to helping strengthen communication and ensure staff voices are heard. Lisa Pappas My name is Lisa Pappas. I work in the Administration, Finance, and Operations office as an Executive Assistant to the Senior Vice President. I will have my third-year anniversary in May. I started in the General Counsel’s office and then moved to my current position in June 2023. I am honored to have been nominated to serve on the Staff Senate and would appreciate the opportunity to be a representative. Savannah Paschal Hi! My name is Savannah Paschal, and I am very excited about the possibility of serving on the Staff Senate. I work in the Department of Modern and Classical Languages and Literatures as a program manager at Alce su Voz. I've been working with Wichita State University for almost two years, but before that, I had just graduated with a bachelor's in Spanish Education here at WSU! I deeply appreciate being nominated, and I will do my best to represent all staff if I serve on the Staff Senate. Lyndsay Pletcher Name, Department, Position My name is Lyndsay Pletcher, I work in the Budget Office within the VP of Finance, Admin, and Operations Office. Time at WSU I have worked at WSU for 8.5 years, starting in Human Resources, and transferred to the Budget Office in 2021. Interest in Serving I have truly enjoyed being a part of the Senate for the past two years, it is amazing to be a part of something from the initial idea stage, and watch it come true. I have been lucky to be a part of planning the first two years of the Shocker STRIVE conference, I and am excited to watch that continue to grow and would love to be involved in the continued planning of that if I were to be voted as a Senator for a second term. Sadi Roberts Hello! My name is Sadi Roberts. I’m honored to be nominated to serve on Staff Senate. I currently serve in Human Resources as the Learning and Development Specialist. I’ve been with Wichita State University for a year and a half. Prior to joining WSU, I worked for a large tech care company for 18 years leading successful teams and building leadership development programs. I’m interested in serving on Staff Senate to be a connection point and advocate for my fellow colleagues. My hope is to continue to build relationships across campus, learn what feedback and ideas you have for elevating our workplace culture, and help implement strategies and solutions that benefit us all. Teri Robertson I’ve worked at WSU for 5 years and have gained valuable experience in finance and day-to-day operations to connect students with employers. I’m passionate about representing and advocating for the interests of all staff members. I strive to create a positive and inclusive work environment where staff feel valued and supported and I would like the opportunity to expand that drive across campus. Eiran Saucedo-Rodarte Buenas! My name is Eiran Saucedo-Rodarte (he/el) and I'm grateful to be nominated to serve on the Staff Senate at WSU. Currently, I work in the Office of Student Success: First-Year Programs overseeing the orientation process for all new undergraduate Shockers. On campus, you'll also find me involved as the President of the Latine Faculty & Staff Association, Member of the First-Generation Coordinating Council, and a Member of the Campus Climate Committee. Through my various involvements, I've found a deep passion in understanding and addressing the needs and concerns of Faculty/Staff at WSU. Serving on the Staff Senate would provide an opportunity to advocate meaningful changes that enhance workplace experiences for all employees, particularly those who have been historically underrepresented and disengaged while at WSU. I hope to foster a supportive and empowering environment for all - contributing to initiatives that improve workplace climate, staff well-being, and professional development opportunities. Preston Schroeder Hi! My name is Preston Schroeder. I am the Director of Investigations for Wichita State University’s Office of Civil Rights, Title IX & ADA Compliance (CTAC). I have been with WSU for about two years. I served as the Assistant Director of CTAC before being promoted to my current position. I previously worked for Sedgwick County for 15 years, with a focus on professional standards and investigative procedures. During my time as an undergraduate and graduate student at Wichita State University, I preferred to stay engaged and was active as a Student Ambassador, a Barton School Dean’s Ambassador, and as a member of Sigma Phi Epsilon. As a staff member, I want to continue being active and engaged at Wichita State. Through my role in CTAC and as a member of the CARE Team, I assist students, faculty, and staff with varying issues they are experiencing. I believe being a member of Staff Senate will allow me the opportunity to continue assisting and giving back to our campus partners in another manner. Go Shocks! Jeffrey Severin My name is Jeff Severin, and I am a Senior Program Manager for the Environmental Finance Center (EFC), a program withing the Hugo Wall School of Public Affairs. I have served as Associate Director of the Heartland Environmental Justice Center from the time it was established at the EFC in July of 2023. In this role, I am part of a team that supports non-profit organizations and small municipalities throughout Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska, and the 9 adjoining Indigenous Nations, as they address local environmental challenges and work to improve quality of life for their community members. I joined the Environmental Finance Center in 2021 as a fully remote employee working from Lawrence, KS. With infrequent visits to campus, and in a role that is very external, it can be difficult to feel connected to well-represented at WSU. I believe I can represent a segment of our campus that can relate – whether they are working remotely like me or working on campus with a focus on off-campus communities in Wichita and beyond – while also representing more traditional on-campus staff. Although I have worked for WSU for just over 4 years, I have been employed in higher education in Kansas for 21 years in roles that bridged academics, administration, operations, student affairs, and community engagement and interacted with campus leadership. I also served on staff senate at a previous institution, including 4 years as the Diversity and Inclusion Committee Co-chair, a position that served on the Staff Senate Executive Committee. Throughout my career as a manager and leader, I have always focused on improving the work environment and the health and well-being of fellow staff members. As your senator, I would draw on this experience and bring that same focus to Staff Senate. Kelley Smetak Hello, my name is Kelley Smetak. I am the Operations and Financial Director for Academic Affairs. I have been in banking and finance since I graduated from KU. I have enjoyed worked here at WSU for the last 8 or so years. I am also a WSU graduate, having received my MPA from the Hugo Wall School of Public Affairs in 2022. I think it is important to have a voice that will speak up on behalf of all the staff here at WSU. Rachel Tuck I have been a dedicated member of the University community since Fall 2011. I started my journey as a student employee in SAC before transferring to the Honors College, gaining valuable insights and experiences along the way. In 2015, I accepted the full-time position as Assistant Rowing Coach in Campus Recreation. I am thrilled to join the Staff Senate, where I look forward to sharing my experiences and advocating for the employees I represent, if selected. My goal is to ensure that every voice is heard and to contribute positively to our University's growth and success. Jeremy Webster Hello there! My name is Jeremy Webster, and I’m Website Manager on the Web Services team, working out of the Media Resources Center. I’ve been with WSU since April 8 (my wife’s birthday) of 2019, almost six years now. Over the years I’ve worked with many staff and faculty from across the entirety of WSU, and I enjoy helping those who reach out to me tackle their challenges and meet their goals. I would like to extend that spirit of community service and cooperation in a position on the Staff Senate if given the opportunity. I’m grateful for the nomination and, should I be elected, look forward to serving on the Faculty Senate and representing the staff here at Wichita State University. Christopher Wiebe Hello, my name is Chris Wiebe, and I work in Housing and Residence Life as the Assistant Director of Educational Engagement. I have been at WSU for three years now. I am interested in serving on the University Staff Senate because WSU gave me so much in the past when I went to school here, and I had a great time when I was a Resident Assistant for Housing. The staff at WSU helped me find my path to my future going into Student Affairs, and I want to give back to the University. I am also interested in serving on the staff senate because I want to make new connections, learn how to share my pride for this institution and help shape the future of WSU. If voted into the Staff Senate, I will support diversity and inclusion across campus, ensuring everyone has a voice. I will be open to hearing everyone and bringing new ideas and ways of thinking. Brandy Willett Angela Zeorlin I have been part of the Wichita State University community since 2002. Once on campus, I couldn’t resist the temptation to complete my college education and fell in love with learning all over again. I am currently the Associate Director for Scholarships where I work more directly with the management end of the scholarship processes while being a mentor and general financial aid “go-to” for our campus. In my role, I have the opportunity to work with campus partners from every entity, leadership in Morrison Hall, Deans and Department Chairs, administrative support staff, the WSU Foundation and Alumni Engagement, research partners, students, and families. These interactions allow me to understand varying viewpoints and gain a working knowledge of operations as a whole. I have also served on several boards and committees in my field from both the State and Regional level. I would be honored to bring my expertise to the service of the University Staff Senate to help us all reach the shared goals of Wichita State University. Non-Exempt Anastasia Allen Anastasia Allen, University Libraries - Library Scholarly Information Specialist I have worked at WSU for a year starting in October of 2023. With my position I am fortunate enough to process and collect evidence for our University's accreditation and because of this I feel a deep connection to the colleges' staff who wish to see WSU succeed. I hope to be a model representative of Wichita State staff as well as be a voice for all staff members across WSU. Estella Armenta Your name, Department you work in and position Estella Armenta, Undergraduate Research and Creative Activity Hub (UReCA), a Unit under the Dorothy and Bill Cohen Honors College, I am the Academic Program Specialist How long have you worked at WSU I have been in this position since January 2025. I completed my Undergraduate career here in Fall 2023 and I am continuing my graduate studies here. I graduate in May 2026. Why you are interested in serving I'm interested in serving fellow staff to increase my network and advocate for and speak up for staff who do not feel comfortable speaking up or showing up. What you hope to accomplish I want to help shape programs for undergraduate students for research opportunities. I also want to create a space/group for staff members throughout the campus, that is welcoming, that meets a few times a semester and puts on fun and informative events for WSU Staff. I don't know if this is already a thing, but I am sure I will gain more information as I go. LaShawna Bale My name is LaShawna Bale, and I currently serve as the Administrative Specialist for the department of Anthropology. I have been with Wichita State University for 6 months and have had an exciting time learning all the intricate mysteries of WSU - and still learning! My core values are integrity, growth, and service. I am a proud Air Force Veteran and hold an MA in Human Resources Management. I am interested in serving to learn the business, provide a fresh perspective to the group, while advancing the mission of Wichita State University. With an ever-changing work environment, it is important we continue making improvements and implementing changes that are positive and impact everyone for the greater good. I feel honored to be nominated and look forward to being a part of this spirited community. Bryant Belden Angela Blackerby Hello, I’m Angela Blackerby and I’m honored to be nominated. I have been the Aerospace Engineering Advisor since 2017. I help support enrollment, retention, and recruiting of approximately 450 Aerospace Engineering undergraduate students, and I truly enjoy working with students. I’m interested in serving on Staff Senate because in my daily job I advocate for students, and I would like to stretch that skillset into advocating for staff. I hope to make a positive change for staff members, make more University connections, and learn more about Wichita State in the process of being a Senator. Katherine Brewster Hello, My name is Katherine (Kat) Brewster, and I currently serve as an Academic Advisor for the School of Computing in the College of Engineering at Wichita State University. I've been part of the WSU community for just over a year and recently completed my Master's in Academic Advising from Kansas State University in May 2024. I have a deep passion for helping students navigate their career paths and thrive in their achievements. I am truly honored to have been nominated for a seat on the Staff Senate. I believe it's essential for dedicated staff members to advocate for what's best for the WSU community. I am eager to serve on the Staff Senate to represent staff interest, collaborate with colleagues, foster a positive workplace culture, and support personal and professional development. Wendy Brooking Name, Department, Position Wendy Brooking, School of Computing, Office Coordinator Time at WSU 3 years and 5 months Interest in Serving I desire to serve others by representing their concerns to the Senate. What I Hope to Accomplish In my capacity as a Senate member, I hope that I will become a source of information and assistance to those across the university. I intend to give staff a voice that will represent their concerns. Kaytie Brozek Lawrence Compton Hi, I'm Larry Compton and I am the Student Success Coach for the College of Fine Arts. I have been at WSU for just over 2 years. I appreciate the nomination to run for Staff Senate and have accepted it because I believe it is important to do my part to continue to provide representation for the WSU staff. My goal as a staff senator would be to be a part of an important group of colleagues that effectively works to help provide staff with the best support and assistance we can give them in order to create the best possible University experience for our students. Stefanie Coronado Stefanie Coronado, Office of Student Success, Lead Success Coach, College of Engineering I have been at WSU since November 2020. The reason I want to be involved is the continued effort to be an advocate for changes and/or improvement across campus. The hope is that being involved in staff senate would pave a way to further collaboration across campus. Kayla Cunningham Jennifer Eastham Hello, my name is Jenny Eastham. I have worked at Wichita State in the Office of International Education in various roles for the last 10 years and am currently serving as an International Admissions Evaluator and Transfer Credit Coordinator where I have the opportunity to work collaboratively with many other departments across campus. I am interested in serving because I understand the importance of collaboration and fostering a positive and productive work environment that benefits not only staff and faculty but also Wichita State as a whole, as well as the Wichita community. I want to be a voice for staff concerns, promote transparency in decision-making, and help improve policies that impact my fellow staff members. If elected, I hope to advocate for policies that enhance the workplace experience, staff effectiveness, and university operations. I hope to make an impact by encouraging confidence and security in WSU’s mission by helping our staff feel supported, informed, and empowered. Heather Hill John Keckeisen Hi! My name is John Keckeisen. I currently serve as the Office Coordinator for the History department in the Fairmount College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. I have been with Wichita State for just over six years, having started as the Administrative Specialist in the School of Criminal Justice. I am also a Shocker alum, receiving my Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from WSU. Having previously served as President of the LAS Staff Advisory Council, I gained an appreciation for representing my fellow staff members and enjoyed being a liaison between them and university leaders. I hope to bring that same level of appreciation to the staff body as a whole on the University Staff Senate. I am grateful for the opportunity to be nominated. Barbara Myers Barb Myers earned a Master of Arts in Liberal Science in 2020 from Wichita State University. During her time as a graduate student, she founded and managed a local non-profit responsible for cemetery preservation and worked as a graduate teaching assistant. Barb joined the WSU staff full-time in October 2024 and is currently the Administrative Specialist in the School of Art, Design and Creative Industries, in the College of Fine Arts. Barb’s goal is to help facilitate the lines of communication at WSU by creating more opportunities for interaction between staff from different departments on campus. She also seeks to encourage improved communication between staff and university leadership by advocating for increased participation in existing projects and committees. Jessica Pierpoint Hello! My name is Jessica Pierpoint. I am grateful to be re-nominated to serve on Staff Senate. Currently, I work at Ablah Library as the Patent and Trademark Specialist. I have been with Wichita State University since January 2019, a little over 4 years. I have had the opportunity to serve on the Staff Senate since 2021, acting as Co-Chair of the Staff Awards and Recognition Committee for this past year. I truly enjoy the higher educational environment and community that Wichita State offers and have always had a passion to make our university and community greater. I look forward to the opportunity to continue being a representative for WSU Staff and am honored to be nominated. Margaret Rees Hello, my name is Margaret Rees. I am an Administrative Specialist at the School of Computing in the College of Engineering. I have been working at Wichita State University for 3 years, the first year as a temp. I love the way my job leads me to reaching out to all kinds of people with varied skills across the university, as well as giving me the opportunity to contribute towards the students’ lives. I have been living in the United States for 4 years, having emigrated from Zimbabwe, where I taught English to high school students. I envision being part of the Staff Senate as positive opportunity to understand relationships and decisions across campus and be part of a team that sees that expectations are met. Marco Villela Department and Position: Office of Online & Adult Learning, Retention Specialist How long have you worked at WSU : 3 Years and 8 Months Why you are interested in serving : I am interested in serving on the Staff Senate because I want to bring fresh, innovative, and confident legislative recommendations to elevate the respect, benefits, and overall morale of staff across all university departments. What you hope to accomplish : My goals are to eliminate inefficiencies, address issues, and represent and protect staff across the university, ensuring that all staff members, regardless of their position, receive the benefits they deserve.
